Alert me to new notifications with a tab icon badge and opt-in desktop notifications

enhancement,scope: medium
CarsonRackley
Part of #7. Upstream requests: go-gitea/gitea#1415 (badge on the favicon) and go-gitea/gitea#31925 (browser notifications).

### User Story

As a user who keeps Gitea open in a background tab, I want the tab icon to show when I have unread notifications, and optionally a desktop notification when a new one arrives, so that I notice review requests and mentions without switching back to check.

### User Scenario

Marco keeps Gitea open in one of many browser tabs while he codes. On the Notifications page he clicks "Enable desktop notifications", and the browser asks for permission once. He allows it. Later a teammate requests his review. A dot appears on the Gitea tab's icon, and a desktop notification says "You have 1 new notification". He clicks it, and the browser switches to Gitea and opens his notifications. After he reads it, the unread count drops to zero and the dot disappears. When he is already looking at Gitea, no desktop notification pops up; the navbar count is enough.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given a signed-in user with at least one unread notification, when any Gitea page loads or the unread count updates, then the tab icon shows a badge dot, and when the count drops to 0 the default icon comes back without a reload.
- [ ] AC2: Given an Actions run page, which already sets the tab icon to the run's status, when the user also has unread notifications, then the run status icon is shown, not the notification badge.
- [ ] AC3: Given desktop notifications have never been enabled in this browser, when new notifications arrive, then no desktop notification is shown and the browser never asks for permission on its own.
- [ ] AC4: Given the user clicks "Enable desktop notifications" on the Notifications page, when the browser asks for permission and the user denies it, then the page says notifications are blocked by the browser and the setting stays off.
- [ ] AC5: Given desktop notifications are enabled and permission is granted, when the unread count goes up while the Gitea tab is hidden, then exactly one desktop notification is shown saying how many new notifications there are, without the issue title or repository name.
- [ ] AC6: Given Gitea is open in several tabs, when the unread count goes up, then the user gets one desktop notification, not one per tab.
- [ ] AC7: Given the Gitea tab is visible, or the count stays the same or goes down, when the count updates, then no desktop notification is shown.
- [ ] AC8: Given a desktop notification is shown, when the user clicks it, then the browser focuses Gitea and opens `/notifications`.
- [ ] AC9: Given desktop notifications are enabled, when the user clicks "Disable desktop notifications", then no more desktop notifications are shown in that browser.

### Out of Scope

- Notifications when no Gitea tab is open (Web Push with a service worker and server-side keys).
- A number inside the badge, or a count in the page title.
- Per-type or per-repository rules for which notifications alert.
- Sounds, email, and the mobile or API side of notifications.

### Open Questions

- Should the badge be something the user can turn off? (Proposed: no. It is passive and only appears when there is something unread.)
- Should the alert also fire when the page falls back to polling because the event stream is unavailable? (Proposed: yes, both update paths behave the same.)

### Design Decisions

#### Decision 1: The desktop notification opt-in is stored per browser, not on the account

**Decision:** "Enable desktop notifications" is remembered in the browser's local storage.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) A per-user setting stored on the server, shown in Settings. (b) No stored setting: alert whenever the browser permission is granted.
**Rationale:** Browser permission is per browser and per device anyway, and browsers only allow the permission prompt after a click. A server-side setting would turn on in a browser that never granted permission and would have to prompt without a click, which browsers block. With (b), users who granted permission for something else could not turn the alerts off without revoking it.
**Consequences:** No server or schema change. The choice does not follow the user to other browsers, and clearing site data turns it off.

#### Decision 2: The desktop notification shows only a count

**Decision:** The notification text is "You have N new notifications" and clicking it opens `/notifications`.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Show the newest notification's issue title and repository. (b) Show one notification per new item, each linking to its issue.
**Rationale:** The live update only delivers a count, so (a) and (b) need an extra API request per update. Titles from private repositories would also appear on a lock screen or a shared screen. A count is enough to make the user switch tabs.
**Consequences:** The user cannot tell a review request from a subscription update until they open Gitea. Richer content is follow-up work if users ask for it.

#### Decision 3: Badge as a dot, with Actions run status taking precedence

**Decision:** The badge is a plain dot drawn on the Gitea icon, reusing the drawing code that already badges the icon with an Actions run's status. On a run page the run status wins.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Draw the unread number in the icon. (b) Put the count in the page title, like "(3) Gitea".
**Rationale:** A number is unreadable at 16 px and needs a "9+" cap. The title is truncated in a crowded tab bar and changes the text screen readers announce. On a run page the user is watching that run, so its status is the more useful icon.
**Consequences:** The icon code needs to know which badge currently owns the icon, so leaving a run page or reading every notification restores the right one.

### Scope

medium

---

import {GET} from '../modules/fetch.ts';
import {toggleElem, createElementFromHTML} from '../utils/dom.ts';
import {UserEventsSharedWorker} from '../modules/worker.ts';

const {appSubUrl, notificationSettings} = window.config;
let notificationSequenceNumber = 0;

async function receiveUpdateCount(event: MessageEvent<{type: string, data: string}>) {
  try {
    const data = JSON.parse(event.data.data);
    for (const count of document.querySelectorAll('.notification_count')) {
      count.classList.toggle('tw-hidden', data.Count === 0);
      count.textContent = String(data.Count);
    }
    await updateNotificationTable();
  } catch (error) {
    console.error(error, event);
  }
}

export function initNotificationCount() {
  if (!document.querySelector('.notification_count')) return;

  let usingPeriodicPoller = false;
  const startPeriodicPoller = (timeout: number, lastCount?: number) => {
    if (timeout <= 0 || !Number.isFinite(timeout)) return;
    usingPeriodicPoller = true;
    lastCount = lastCount ?? getCurrentCount();
    setTimeout(async () => {
      await updateNotificationCountWithCallback(startPeriodicPoller, timeout, lastCount);
    }, timeout);
  };

  if (notificationSettings.EventSourceUpdateTime > 0 && window.EventSource && window.SharedWorker) {
    // Try to connect to the event source via the shared worker first
    const worker = new UserEventsSharedWorker('notification-worker');
    worker.addMessageEventListener((event: MessageEvent) => {
      if (event.data.type === 'no-event-source') {
        if (!usingPeriodicPoller) startPeriodicPoller(notificationSettings.MinTimeout);
      } else if (event.data.type === 'notification-count') {
        receiveUpdateCount(event); // no await
      }
    });
    worker.startPort();
    return;
  }

  startPeriodicPoller(notificationSettings.MinTimeout);
}

function getCurrentCount() {
  return Number(document.querySelector('.notification_count')!.textContent ?? '0');
}

async function updateNotificationCountWithCallback(callback: (timeout: number, newCount: number) => void, timeout: number, lastCount: number) {
  const currentCount = getCurrentCount();
  if (lastCount !== currentCount) {
    callback(notificationSettings.MinTimeout, currentCount);
    return;
  }

  const newCount = await updateNotificationCount();
  let needsUpdate = false;

  if (lastCount !== newCount) {
    needsUpdate = true;
    timeout = notificationSettings.MinTimeout;
  } else if (timeout < notificationSettings.MaxTimeout) {
    timeout += notificationSettings.TimeoutStep;
  }

  callback(timeout, newCount);
  if (needsUpdate) {
    await updateNotificationTable();
  }
}

async function updateNotificationTable() {
  const notificationDiv = document.querySelector('#notification_div');
  if (!notificationDiv) return;

  try {
    const params = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search);
    params.set('div-only', 'true');
    params.set('sequence-number', String(++notificationSequenceNumber));
    const response = await GET(`${appSubUrl}/notifications?${params.toString()}`);

    if (!response.ok) {
      throw new Error('Failed to fetch notification table');
    }

    const data = await response.text();
    const el = createElementFromHTML(data);
    if (parseInt(el.getAttribute('data-sequence-number')!) === notificationSequenceNumber) {
      const flash = notificationDiv.querySelector('.flash-message');
      notificationDiv.outerHTML = data;
      // the page load already consumed the flash, so the refreshed list would drop e.g. a bulk action's confirmation
      const container = document.querySelector('#notification_div > .ui.container')!;
      if (flash && !container.querySelector('.flash-message')) container.prepend(flash);
    }
  } catch (error) {
    console.error(error);
  }
}

async function updateNotificationCount(): Promise<number> {
  try {
    const response = await GET(`${appSubUrl}/notifications/new`);

    if (!response.ok) {
      throw new Error('Failed to fetch notification count');
    }

    const data = await response.json();

    toggleElem('.notification_count', data.new !== 0);

    for (const el of document.querySelectorAll('.notification_count')) {
      el.textContent = String(data.new);
    }

    return data.new as number;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error(error);
    return 0;
  }
}
import {getActionStatusIcon} from './action-status-icon.ts';
import type {ActionsStatus} from './gitea-actions.ts';
import {svgParseOuterInner} from '../svg.ts';
import {html, htmlRaw} from '../utils/html.ts';

const {svgOuter, svgInnerHtml: giteaFaviconInner} = svgParseOuterInner('gitea-favicon');
const faviconViewBox = svgOuter.getAttribute('viewBox')!;
const [, , faviconViewBoxWidth, faviconViewBoxHeight] = faviconViewBox.split(/\s+/).map(Number);

// the status badge is rendered in the bottom-right corner, following GitHub Actions favicon proportions
const badgeIconSize = 16;
const badgeSizeRatio = 340 / 640;
const badgeMargin = 6;
const badgeDrawSize = faviconViewBoxWidth * badgeSizeRatio;
const badgeX = faviconViewBoxWidth - badgeDrawSize - badgeMargin;
const badgeY = faviconViewBoxHeight - badgeDrawSize - badgeMargin;
const badgeScale = badgeDrawSize / badgeIconSize;
// white ring behind the badge so it stands out from the logo, like GitHub's favicon
const badgeCenter = badgeDrawSize / 2;
const badgeRingRadius = badgeCenter + badgeDrawSize * 0.08;

let currentStatus: ActionsStatus | null = null;
const defaultFaviconHrefs = new Map<HTMLLinkElement, string>();
const faviconDataUrlCache = new Map<ActionsStatus, string>();
let colorProbe: HTMLElement | null = null;

function rememberDefaultFaviconHrefs() {
  if (defaultFaviconHrefs.size > 0) return;
  for (const link of document.querySelectorAll<HTMLLinkElement>('link[rel~="icon"]')) {
    defaultFaviconHrefs.set(link, link.href);
  }
}

function resolveTailwindTextColor(colorClass: string): string {
  if (!colorProbe) {
    colorProbe = document.createElement('span');
    colorProbe.style.display = 'none';
    document.body.append(colorProbe);
  }
  colorProbe.className = colorClass;
  return getComputedStyle(colorProbe).color || '#000000';
}

function buildStatusIconMarkup(status: ActionsStatus): string {
  const {name, colorClass} = getActionStatusIcon(status, 'circle-fill');
  const color = resolveTailwindTextColor(colorClass);
  const {svgInnerHtml} = svgParseOuterInner(name);
  const coloredInner = svgInnerHtml.replaceAll('currentColor', color);
  const ring = html`<circle cx="${badgeX + badgeCenter}" cy="${badgeY + badgeCenter}" r="${badgeRingRadius}" fill="#ffffff"/>`;
  const badge = html`<g data-actions-status-name="${status}" transform="translate(${badgeX}, ${badgeY}) scale(${badgeScale})" fill="${color}" color="${color}">${htmlRaw(coloredInner)}</g>`;
  return html`${htmlRaw(ring)}${htmlRaw(badge)}`;
}

export function buildStatusFaviconSvg(status: ActionsStatus): string {
  return html`<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="${faviconViewBox}">${htmlRaw(giteaFaviconInner)}${htmlRaw(buildStatusIconMarkup(status))}</svg>`;
}

function buildStatusFaviconDataUrl(status: ActionsStatus): string {
  const cached = faviconDataUrlCache.get(status);
  if (cached) return cached;
  const dataUrl = `data:image/svg+xml,${encodeURIComponent(buildStatusFaviconSvg(status))}`;
  faviconDataUrlCache.set(status, dataUrl);
  return dataUrl;
}

function setFaviconHref(href: string) {
  rememberDefaultFaviconHrefs();
  for (const link of defaultFaviconHrefs.keys()) {
    if (link.isConnected) link.href = href;
  }
}

export function syncActionRunFavicon(status: ActionsStatus | ''): void {
  if (status === '') {
    resetActionFavicon();
    return;
  }
  if (status === currentStatus) return;
  setFaviconHref(buildStatusFaviconDataUrl(status));
  currentStatus = status;
}

export function resetActionFavicon(): void {
  if (currentStatus === null) return;
  rememberDefaultFaviconHrefs();
  for (const [link, href] of defaultFaviconHrefs) {
    if (link.isConnected) link.href = href;
  }
  currentStatus = null;
}

const {appSubUrl, sharedWorkerUri} = window.config;

export class UserEventsSharedWorker {
  sharedWorker: SharedWorker;

  // options can be either a string (the debug name of the worker) or an object of type WorkerOptions
  constructor(options?: string | WorkerOptions) {
    const worker = new SharedWorker(sharedWorkerUri, options);
    this.sharedWorker = worker;
    worker.addEventListener('error', (event) => {
      console.error('worker error', event);
    });
    worker.port.addEventListener('messageerror', () => {
      console.error('unable to deserialize message');
    });
    worker.port.postMessage({
      type: 'start',
      url: `${window.location.origin}${appSubUrl}/user/events`,
    });
    worker.port.addEventListener('error', (e) => {
      console.error('worker port error', e);
    });
    window.addEventListener('beforeunload', () => {
      // FIXME: this logic is not quite right.
      // "beforeunload" can be canceled by some actions like "are-you-sure" and the navigation can be cancelled.
      // In this case: the worker port is incorrectly closed while the page is still there.
      worker.port.postMessage({type: 'close'});
      worker.port.close();
    });
  }

  addMessageEventListener(listener: (event: MessageEvent) => void) {
    this.sharedWorker.port.addEventListener('message', (event: MessageEvent) => {
      if (!event.data || !event.data.type) {
        console.error('unknown worker message event', event);
        return;
      }

      if (event.data.type === 'error') {
        console.error('worker port event error', event.data);
      } else if (event.data.type === 'logout') {
        if (event.data.data !== 'here') return;
        this.sharedWorker.port.postMessage({type: 'close'});
        this.sharedWorker.port.close();
        // slightly delay our "logout" for a short while, in case there are other logout requests in-flight.
        // * if the logout is triggered by a page redirection (e.g.: user clicks "/user/logout")
        //   * "beforeunload" event is triggered, this code path won't execute
        // * if the logout is triggered by a fetch call
        //   * "beforeunload" event is not triggered until JS does the redirection.
        //     * in this case, the logout fetch call already completes and has sent the "logout" message to the worker
        //   * there can be a data-race between the fetch call's redirection and the "logout" message from the worker
        //     * the fetch call's logout redirection should always win over the worker message, because it might have a custom location
        setTimeout(() => { window.location.assign(`${appSubUrl}/`) }, 1000);
      } else if (event.data.type === 'close') {
        this.sharedWorker.port.postMessage({type: 'close'});
        this.sharedWorker.port.close();
      }
      listener(event);
    });
  }

  startPort() {
    this.sharedWorker.port.start();
  }
}

class Source {
  url: string;
  eventSource: EventSource | null;
  listening: Record<string, boolean>;
  clients: Array<MessagePort>;

  constructor(url: string) {
    this.url = url;
    this.eventSource = new EventSource(url);
    this.listening = {};
    this.clients = [];
    this.listen('open');
    this.listen('close');
    this.listen('logout');
    this.listen('notification-count');
    this.listen('stopwatches');
    this.listen('error');
  }

  register(port: MessagePort) {
    if (this.clients.includes(port)) return;

    this.clients.push(port);

    port.postMessage({
      type: 'status',
      message: `registered to ${this.url}`,
    });
  }

  deregister(port: MessagePort) {
    const portIdx = this.clients.indexOf(port);
    if (portIdx < 0) {
      return this.clients.length;
    }
    this.clients.splice(portIdx, 1);
    return this.clients.length;
  }

  close() {
    if (!this.eventSource) return;

    this.eventSource.close();
    this.eventSource = null;
  }

  listen(eventType: string) {
    if (this.listening[eventType]) return;
    this.listening[eventType] = true;
    this.eventSource?.addEventListener(eventType, (event) => {
      this.notifyClients({
        type: eventType,
        data: event.data,
      });
    });
  }

  notifyClients(event: {type: string, data: any}) {
    for (const client of this.clients) {
      client.postMessage(event);
    }
  }

  status(port: MessagePort) {
    port.postMessage({
      type: 'status',
      message: `url: ${this.url} readyState: ${this.eventSource?.readyState}`,
    });
  }
}

const sourcesByUrl = new Map<string, Source | null>();
const sourcesByPort = new Map<MessagePort, Source | null>();

(self as unknown as SharedWorkerGlobalScope).addEventListener('connect', (e: MessageEvent) => {
  for (const port of e.ports) {
    port.addEventListener('message', (event: MessageEvent) => {
      if (!self.EventSource) {
        // some browsers (like PaleMoon, Firefox<53) don't support EventSource in SharedWorkerGlobalScope.
        // this event handler needs EventSource when doing "new Source(url)", so just post a message back to the caller,
        // in case the caller would like to use a fallback method to do its work.
        port.postMessage({type: 'no-event-source'});
        return;
      }
      if (event.data.type === 'start') {
        const url = event.data.url;
        let source = sourcesByUrl.get(url);
        if (source) {
          // we have a Source registered to this url
          source.register(port);
          sourcesByPort.set(port, source);
          return;
        }
        source = sourcesByPort.get(port);
        if (source) {
          if (source.eventSource && source.url === url) return;

          // How this has happened I don't understand...
          // deregister from that source
          const count = source.deregister(port);
          // Clean-up
          if (count === 0) {
            source.close();
            sourcesByUrl.set(source.url, null);
          }
        }
        // Create a new Source
        source = new Source(url);
        source.register(port);
        sourcesByUrl.set(url, source);
        sourcesByPort.set(port, source);
      } else if (event.data.type === 'listen') {
        const source = sourcesByPort.get(port)!;
        source.listen(event.data.eventType);
      } else if (event.data.type === 'close') {
        const source = sourcesByPort.get(port);
        if (!source) return;

        const count = source.deregister(port);
        if (count === 0) {
          source.close();
          sourcesByUrl.set(source.url, null);
          sourcesByPort.set(port, null);
        }
      } else if (event.data.type === 'status') {
        const source = sourcesByPort.get(port);
        if (!source) {
          port.postMessage({
            type: 'status',
            message: 'not connected',
          });
          return;
        }
        source.status(port);
      } else {
        // just send it back
        port.postMessage({
          type: 'error',
          message: `received but don't know how to handle: ${event.data}`,
        });
      }
    });
    port.start();
  }
});

/* eslint-disable no-restricted-globals */
// Some people deploy Gitea under a subpath, so it needs prefix to avoid local storage key conflicts.
// And these keys are for user settings only, it also needs a specific prefix,
// in case in the future there are other uses of local storage, and/or we need to clear some keys when the quota is exceeded.
const itemKeyPrefix = 'gitea:setting:';

function handleLocalStorageError(e: any) {
  // in the future, maybe we need to handle quota exceeded errors differently
  console.error('Error using local storage for user settings', e);
}

function getLocalStorageUserSetting(settingKey: string): string | null {
  const legacyKey = settingKey;
  const itemKey = `${itemKeyPrefix}${settingKey}`;
  try {
    const legacyValue = localStorage?.getItem(legacyKey) ?? null;
    const value = localStorage?.getItem(itemKey) ?? null; // avoid undefined
    if (value !== null && legacyValue !== null) {
      // if both values exist, remove the legacy one
      localStorage?.removeItem(legacyKey);
    } else if (value === null && legacyValue !== null) {
      // migrate legacy value to new key
      localStorage?.removeItem(legacyKey);
      localStorage?.setItem(itemKey, legacyValue);
      return legacyValue;
    }
    return value;
  } catch (e) {
    handleLocalStorageError(e);
  }
  return null;
}

function setLocalStorageUserSetting(settingKey: string, value: string) {
  const legacyKey = settingKey;
  const itemKey = `${itemKeyPrefix}${settingKey}`;
  try {
    localStorage?.removeItem(legacyKey);
    localStorage?.setItem(itemKey, value);
  } catch (e) {
    handleLocalStorageError(e);
  }
}

export const localUserSettings = {
  getString: (key: string, def: string = ''): string => {
    return getLocalStorageUserSetting(key) ?? def;
  },
  setString: (key: string, value: string) => {
    setLocalStorageUserSetting(key, value);
  },
  getBoolean: (key: string, def: boolean = false): boolean => {
    return localUserSettings.getString(key, String(def)) === 'true';
  },
  setBoolean: (key: string, value: boolean) => {
    localUserSettings.setString(key, String(value));
  },
  getJsonObject: <T extends Record<string, any>>(key: string, def: T): T => {
    const value = getLocalStorageUserSetting(key);
    try {
      const decoded = value !== null ? JSON.parse(value) : null;
      return {...def, ...decoded};
    } catch (e) {
      console.error(`Unable to parse JSON value for local user settings ${key}=${value}`, e);
    }
    return def;
  },
  setJsonObject: <T extends Record<string, any>>(key: string, value: T) => {
    localUserSettings.setString(key, JSON.stringify(value));
  },
};

window.localUserSettings = localUserSettings;

# web_src/js — page features and how they get wired up

**Read when:** adding or changing browser behaviour on a page.
**Not here:** Vue components -> `frontend-vue-components.md`; styling -> `frontend-css.md`; the HTML -> `templates.md`.

## Responsibilities

| Directory | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| `features/` | one file per page or feature (`repo-issue.ts`, `repo-diff.ts`, `repo-code.ts`), plus `features/admin/` and `features/comp/` for shared widgets |
| `modules/` | cross-cutting infrastructure: `fetch.ts`, `init.ts`, `observer.ts`, `i18n.ts`, `toast.ts`, `tippy.ts`, `fomantic.ts`, `clipboard.ts`, `codeeditor/` |
| `utils/` | pure helpers with no DOM assumptions: `dom.ts`, `html.ts`, `url.ts`, `time.ts`, `color.ts`, `string.ts` |
| `markup/`, `render/` | enhancing already-rendered content (anchors, mermaid, math) |
| `webcomponents/` | custom elements such as `relative-time`, `overflow-menu`, `aria-menu` |

## Key files

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `web_src/js/index.ts` | the entry point: imports fomantic and `../css/index.css`, then passes every `initXxx` to `callInitFunctions` |
| `web_src/js/modules/init.ts` | `callInitFunctions`, `InitPerformanceTracer` |
| `web_src/js/modules/observer.ts` | `registerGlobalInitFunc`, `registerGlobalEventFunc`, `registerGlobalSelectorFunc`, `initGlobalSelectorObserver` |
| `web_src/js/modules/fetch.ts` | `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE` |
| `web_src/js/utils/dom.ts` | `showElem`, `hideElem`, `toggleElem`, `queryElems`, `createElementFromHTML` |
| `web_src/js/modules/i18n.ts` | `trN` — the frontend side of the locale system |
| `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.ts` | `registerShortcut` (keys like `'g c'`), `getShortcuts`, and the `<kbd data-shortcut-keys data-shortcut-section>` hints and `onShortcutLink` links that register themselves |

## Conventions & invariants

**Two ways to wire a feature, and new code should prefer the second.**

1. *Page-load init:* export `initFoo()` from a `features/` file and add it to the array in
   `index.ts`. Every function in that array runs on **every** page, so it must find its elements
   and return immediately when they are absent.
2. *Declarative:* `registerGlobalInitFunc('initFoo', (el) => {...})` in the module, and
   `data-global-init="initFoo"` on the element in the template. For clicks,
   `registerGlobalEventFunc('click', 'onFoo', ...)` with `data-global-click="onFoo"`. This covers
   elements added to the DOM later and runs once per element (guarded by an internal
   `_giteaGlobalInited` flag), so re-adding a node does not re-initialise it.

`registerGlobalSelectorFunc(selector, handler)` also exists, but `observer.ts` marks it as "less
efficient and less maintainable" — it is for element types already on many pages, not new work.

- **Ordering rule:** every `registerGlobalInitFunc` must run *before* `initGlobalSelectorObserver`,
  which `index.ts` deliberately calls last. Registering after it throws.
- **One function per element.** `callGlobalInitFunc` in `observer.ts` looks the attribute up as a
  whole string, so `data-global-init` names exactly one function — space-separating two is an open
  TODO there, not a feature. To add behaviour to an element that already has one (the new-issue
  title in `templates/repo/issue/new_form.tmpl` carries `autoFocusEnd`), put the attribute on a
  wrapper and query for the inner element.
- Data fetching goes through the `fetch.ts` wrappers, never a raw `fetch`.
- Show and hide with `.tw-hidden` plus `showElem` / `hideElem` / `toggleElem`. In Vue use
  `v-if`/`v-show` instead (`frontend-vue-components.md`).
- Use `node.getAttribute`, not `node.dataset` (camel-casing surprises), and never bind
  user-provided data onto a DOM node.
- Custom DOM events are prefixed `ce-`, declared as an exported constant next to their emitter —
  see `EventEditorContentChanged` in `features/comp/EditorMarkdown.ts`.
- TypeScript, per `docs/guidelines-frontend.md`: `import type` for type-only imports,
  `@ts-expect-error` over `@ts-ignore`, `!` rather than `?.`/`??` when a value always exists, and
  `async` only on a function that actually awaits.
- One feature per file or directory; ids and classes are kebab-case with 2-3 feature keywords.

## Recipes

**Add behaviour to an element.** Register a global init func in the owning `features/` module and
put `data-global-init="yourFuncName"` on the element in its template. No change to `index.ts`.

**Add a whole-page feature.** New `features/<name>.ts` exporting `initName()`, an early return when
its root element is missing, then add the import and the array entry in `index.ts`.

**Profile a slow page.** `?_ui_performance_trace=1` prints per-init timings; over 500ms is logged.

**Look up an issue by its number.** `matchIssue` (`utils/match.ts`) is the `#` list's search: a
number comes back first (`services/issue/suggestion.go` → `GetSuggestion`), and the current issue
is left out. Keyword matches are limited to the kinds the viewer may read
(`routers/web/repo/issue_suggestions.go`), but the match by number (`GetIssueByIndex`) is not, so a
viewer who can't read pull requests still gets one typed by its number. The duplicate close
reason's preview in `features/repo-issue-status-button.ts` uses it.

**Add a keyboard shortcut.** Call `registerShortcut` (`modules/shortcut.ts`). One given an `element` exists while that element
is in the document, hidden or not; a clash with a live one throws. A link can declare one that follows it (`onShortcutLink`,
`templates/repo/header.tmpl`), live while it's rendered; markup rendered twice (navbar icons, `templates/base/head_navbar.tmpl`)
marks one copy. The `?` dialog (`templates/base/footer.tmpl`) can turn shortcuts off (WCAG 2.1.4); only `alwaysOn` ones still run.

**Run one test file.** `pnpm exec vitest <path-filter>` (`testing.md`).

## Gotchas

- A page-load init without its early return costs every page in Gitea; the 500ms warning catches it.
- Fomantic-UI (jQuery) is vendored and deprecated. Do not build new features on it, and do not mix
  it with Vue — Vue may use its CSS classes but not its JavaScript.
- Which menu to build on, Fomantic dropdown or `<aria-menu>` (`web_src/js/webcomponents/aria-menu.ts`),
  is decided in `web_src/js/modules/fomantic/aria.md`.
- `utils/` is for pure helpers. A function that reaches for `window` or a global selector belongs
  in `modules/` or `features/`.
- A feature can follow a comment box it did not create: the editor's change and upload events
  bubble (`features/comp/EditorMarkdown.ts`, `features/comp/EditorUpload.ts`), and
  `getComboMarkdownEditor` finds the editor, as `features/repo-issue-status-button.ts` does. But
  the editor attaches itself before its async `init` finishes, and calling it before then throws;
  read its textarea until an event arrives.
- Enter on a Fomantic dropdown item only fires a `click` when the item is a link or carries
  `js-aria-clickable` (`web_src/js/modules/fomantic/dropdown.ts`), so a plain click listener on other
  items never hears a keyboard pick. The close reason menu in `templates/repo/issue/view_content.tmpl`
  marks its items; an `<aria-menu>` item needs no class, as Enter and Space call its `click()`.
- After a click on a Fomantic dropdown item, the dropdown keeps the focus, so focusing something
  else from your click handler needs `setTimeout(..., 0)`.
- `createTippy` (`modules/tippy.ts`) moves a popup to `document.body`, so inputs in it leave their
  `<form>` and are not sent. Keep their values in hidden fields inside the form, as the close reason
  popups in `features/repo-issue-status-button.ts` do.

## Related

- `frontend-vue-components.md` — when a feature should be a Vue app instead
- `templates.md` — where `data-global-init` attributes and `pageData` come from
- `frontend-css.md` — `tw-hidden` and the class conventions

# i18n — locale files and translation

**Read when:** adding or changing any user-visible string.
**Not here:** using a key in a template -> `templates.md`; in TypeScript -> `frontend-js.md`.

## Responsibilities

The translated strings and the machinery that looks them up, for both the backend/templates and
the frontend.

## Key files

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `options/locale/locale_en-US.json` | **the only file you edit** — the source of truth |
| `options/locale/locale_<lang>.json` | 28 other locales, all generated from Crowdin |
| `modules/translation/translation.go` | locale loading and lookup; requires the `locale_*.json` naming |
| `modules/translation/i18n/` | the lookup implementation and fallback behaviour |
| `crowdin.yml` | the sync config: source is `locale_en-US.json`, translations land as `locale_%locale%.json` |

## Conventions & invariants

- **Only ever edit `locale_en-US.json`.** Every other locale file is written by Crowdin
  (`crowdin.yml` sets `en-US` as the source). Editing one by hand is overwritten on the next sync,
  and a PR that touches other locale files will be asked to revert them.
- Keys are dotted and grouped by area (`repo.issues.new`, `settings.`, `admin.`). Put a new key
  next to its neighbours rather than at the end.
- Templates use `{{ctx.Locale.Tr "key"}}`, or `TrN` for plurals. TypeScript uses `trN` from
  `web_src/js/modules/i18n.ts`; strings reach the frontend through `window.config.i18n`
  (`templates/base/head_script.tmpl`), which is deliberately limited to general text — anything
  specialised should arrive via an API response, a `data-` attribute, or `pageData`.
- A plural is **two keys** suffixed `_1` and `_n`, both interpolating `%d` — see
  `actions.runs.graph_jobs_count_1` and `_n`. `TrN` and `trN` pick the form from the count.
- A `data-` attribute carrying a translated string to TypeScript is read with `getAttribute` and
  usually named for its use (`data-tooltip-content`, read in `web_src/js/modules/tippy.ts`). Vue
  mounts often use `data-locale-<name>`, as `templates/repo/actions/view_component.tmpl` does for
  both plural forms.
- **Never write a user-visible literal** in a template, a handler, or a `.ts` file.
- Errors whose message reaches the user go through `util.ErrorWrapTranslatable`
  (`modules-util-and-generics.md`), not a plain `fmt.Errorf`.
- `crowdin.yml` sets `skip_untranslated_strings` and `export_only_approved`, so a missing
  translation falls back rather than shipping an empty string.

## Recipes

**Add a string.** Add the key to `options/locale/locale_en-US.json` in the right group, use it via
`ctx.Locale.Tr` or `trN`, and leave the other locale files alone.

**Add a plural.** Two keys named `<key>_1` and `<key>_n` plus `TrN` / `trN`; the count argument
selects the form.

**Add a string the frontend needs.** Prefer a `data-` attribute or `pageData` from the handler.
Only genuinely general text belongs in the global `window.config.i18n` object.

## Gotchas
=====
import {initNotificationBulkActions, loadSelection, saveSelection, selectedCount, setSelected} from './notification-bulk.ts';
import {createElementFromHTML} from '../utils/dom.ts';

// the markup notification_div.tmpl renders for a page of a view
function createNotificationPage(view: string, viewCount: number, ids: string[]) {
  const root = createElementFromHTML<HTMLElement>(`
    <div id="notification_div" data-view-key="${view}" data-view-count="${viewCount}" data-bulk-url="/notifications/bulk">
      <div class="notification-bulk-bar">
        <input type="checkbox" class="notification-checkbox-all">
        <div class="notification-bulk-actions tw-hidden">
          <span><span class="notification-selected-count">0</span> selected</span>
          <a class="notification-select-all-view tw-hidden" href="#">Select all</a>
          <button class="notification-bulk-action" data-action="mark_as_read">Mark as read</button>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div id="notification_table">
        ${ids.map((id) => `<div class="notifications-item"><input type="checkbox" class="notification-checkbox" data-notification-id="${id}"></div>`).join('')}
      </div>
    </div>`);
  initNotificationBulkActions(root);
  const q = <T extends HTMLElement>(selector: string) => root.querySelector<T>(selector)!;
  const row = (id: string) => q<HTMLInputElement>(`.notification-checkbox[data-notification-id="${id}"]`);
  const tick = (el: HTMLInputElement, checked: boolean) => {
    el.checked = checked;
    el.dispatchEvent(new Event('change'));
  };
  return {
    row, tick,
    selectPage: q<HTMLInputElement>('.notification-checkbox-all'),
    actions: q('.notification-bulk-actions'),
    count: () => q('.notification-selected-count').textContent,
    selectAllView: q('.notification-select-all-view'),
  };
}

Explored the code. One design choice needs your call before I write the plan: how to make sure several tabs produce one alert, and none while you're already looking at a Gitea tab (AC6/AC7).

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-11 14:28:50Z)**_

<tool-use data-tool-type="generic" data-tool-name="AskUserQuestion"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **AskUserQuestion**</summary>
**For AC6/AC7 (one desktop alert across many Gitea tabs, and none while any Gitea tab is visible): every tab gets the same unread-count event at the same moment through the shared worker (eventsource.sharedworker.ts). Where should the decision to alert be made?**

Options:
- **Shared worker (Recommended)** - Tabs tell the worker whether they're visible and send their count. The worker sees each count event once, and when the count goes up with no tab visible, it tells exactly one tab to show the alert. The decision logic goes in a small pure module so it can be unit-tested. In the polling fallback (no SharedWorker), each tab decides for itself, and a shared notification tag merges duplicates into one.
- **Per tab + notification tag** - Each hidden tab shows its own alert, all with the same tag, so the browser merges them into one, and a localStorage 'last alerted count' stops repeats. Simpler, and the worker isn't touched. But a hidden tab still alerts while you're looking at a different Gitea tab, which goes against the issue scenario.

**What color should the unread dot on the tab icon be?**

Options:
- **Primary (navbar badge)** - Same --color-primary as the navbar's unread count bubble, so the two badges match.
- **Blue (unread dot)** - Same tw-blue as the 'has unread' dot in the notifications repo filter.
- **Red** - The usual 'attention' color, but Gitea doesn't use it for unread anywhere else.


**Answer:** Shared worker (Recommended), Primary (navbar badge)
</details></tool-use>

# Plan — Issue #118: unread badge on the tab icon + opt-in desktop notifications

## Context
Issue #118 (spec approved by vvchopra, deferred from Sprint 2 to Sprint 3). Users who leave Gitea in a
background tab don't notice new notifications. The issue asks for:
- a dot on the tab icon while anything is unread (AC1), with the Actions run status icon taking priority (AC2)
- desktop notifications that the user turns on per browser, are triggered only by a click, show only
  a count, and fire once across tabs and only when Gitea isn't visible (AC3–AC9)

Concept location (Carson's): `web_src/js/features/notification.ts`, `web_src/js/modules/favicon-status.ts`,
`templates/user/notification/notification_div.tmpl`.

Decisions settled in this session: the **shared worker** decides cross-tab alerts (AC6/AC7). The dot
uses **`--color-primary`**, the same color as the navbar unread bubble.

Branch: `feat/issue-118-notification-alerts` off `main`. The current branch is `chore/tech-showcase-2` and is clean.

## Changes

### 1. `web_src/js/modules/favicon-status.ts`: two badge owners (Decision 3)
- Replace the single `currentStatus` with two state values: `actionStatus: ActionsStatus | null` and `notificationDot: boolean`.
  A private `renderFavicon()` picks one: action status → status icon; else dot → dot icon; else the default hrefs
  (reuse `rememberDefaultFaviconHrefs` / `setFaviconHref`).
- Keep `syncActionRunFavicon` / `resetActionFavicon` signatures, so `RepoActionView.vue` stays unchanged. They now set
  `actionStatus` and call `renderFavicon()`. Leaving a run page brings the dot back when something is unread.
- New `export function syncNotificationFaviconDot(show: boolean)`.
- New `export function buildNotificationFaviconSvg()`: reuses the same badge geometry and white ring
  (`badgeX/badgeY/badgeCenter/badgeRingRadius`), plus a filled `<circle>` in `--color-primary`
  (read through `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement)`). The data URL is cached like `faviconDataUrlCache`.

### 2. `web_src/js/modules/notification-alert.ts` (new, pure, no DOM): cross-tab decision logic
A `NotificationAlertTracker<Tab>` class, generic over the tab key, so the worker passes `MessagePort` and tests pass strings:
- `setTabState(tab, {visible, count})`: the first reported count seeds `lastCount`/`baseline`. When any tab is visible, `baseline = lastCount`.
- `removeTab(tab)`
- `onCount(count): {tab, newCount} | null`. It returns `null` when any tab is visible (AC7; it also moves the baseline up), when
  `count <= lastCount` (AC7), or when no tabs are known. Otherwise it returns **one** tab, the last one that was visible or else the first
  (AC6), with `newCount = count - baseline`, i.e. "new since you last looked". A drop lowers the baseline.

### 3. `web_src/js/eventsource.sharedworker.ts`: wire the tracker into the worker
- Give `Source` an `alertTracker`. In `listen()`, for `notification-count`, also call `onCount(JSON.parse(data).Count)`
  and `postMessage({type: 'notification-alert', count})` to the returned port only.
- New port message `notification-tab-state` → `setTabState`. The existing `close`/deregister path → `removeTab`.
- The stopwatch worker is a separate named SharedWorker and never sends tab state, so it is unaffected.

### 4. `web_src/js/modules/worker.ts`
- Add a small `postMessage(msg)` method on `UserEventsSharedWorker`, so callers don't reach into `sharedWorker.port`.

### 5. `web_src/js/features/notification-desktop.ts` (new): opt-in, toggle and showing the alert
- Setting `notification.desktop-alerts`, stored through `localUserSettings` (`modules/user-settings.ts`). Decision 1: per browser.
- `desktopAlertsEnabled()`: true only when the setting is on **and** `Notification.permission === 'granted'`. A permission revoked later reads as off.
- `showDesktopAlert(newCount)`: `new Notification(title, {body: trN(newCount, form1, formN), tag: 'gitea-notifications', icon})`. Title and text
  come from `data-` attributes on the navbar notification link (below), and the body never includes issue or repo text (AC5).
  `onclick` → `window.focus()`, `window.location.assign(`${appSubUrl}/notifications`)`, `close()` (AC8).
- `registerGlobalInitFunc('initNotificationDesktopToggle', ...)` renders the button state:
  - Notification API missing → hide the button.
  - Setting on → "Disable" label. Clicking turns the setting off (AC9).
  - Setting off and permission `granted` → turn it on. Permission `denied` → show the blocked message.
    Permission `default` → `Notification.requestPermission()` **only inside this click handler** (AC3).
    `granted` → turn on, `denied` → blocked message and stays off (AC4), dismissed → stays off silently.
  - Using global-init matters because `updateNotificationTable()` swaps `#notification_div` through `outerHTML`, so the button gets re-initialised.

### 6. `web_src/js/features/notification.ts`: hook both update paths
- `initNotificationCount()`: call `syncNotificationFaviconDot(getCurrentCount() > 0)` on load (AC1).
- SSE path: after connecting, post `notification-tab-state {visible: document.visibilityState === 'visible', count}`, and again on
  `visibilitychange`. Handle the new `notification-alert` message → `if (desktopAlertsEnabled()) showDesktopAlert(count)`.
- `receiveUpdateCount` and `updateNotificationCount` (poll path) both call `syncNotificationFaviconDot(count > 0)`.
- Poll fallback only (no shared worker, so no coordination): in `updateNotificationCountWithCallback`, when `newCount > lastCount`
  and the tab is hidden, alert with the delta. The shared `tag` merges duplicates across tabs into one notification. This also
  answers the issue's open question with "yes, both paths alert".

### 7. Templates and locale
- `templates/user/notification/notification_div.tmpl`: in the right-hand `flex-text-block`, next to "Group by repository", add a
  wrapper with `data-global-init="initNotificationDesktopToggle"` containing a `ui mini basic button` with the enable and disable labels, plus
  a `tw-hidden` blocked-message span (the JS picks which one shows).
- `templates/base/head_navbar_icons.tmpl`: on the notifications link, add `data-desktop-alert-title="{{AppName}}"`,
  `data-desktop-alert-1` / `-n` (the alert can fire on any page, so the text has to be on every page).
- `options/locale/locale_en-US.json` (edit only this locale; keys go next to the other `notification.*` keys):
  `notification.desktop_enable`, `notification.desktop_disable`, `notification.desktop_blocked`,
  `notification.desktop_alert_1` ("You have %d new notification"), `notification.desktop_alert_n`.

## Tests (unit/vitest; expected values come from the ACs, and all of these are AI-written, to be listed in the PR's Test Evidence)
- `web_src/js/modules/favicon-status.test.ts` (extend): dot shown when unread, default icon back when it drops to 0 (AC1);
  status icon wins over the dot, and resetting the run brings the dot back (AC2).
- `web_src/js/modules/notification-alert.test.ts` (new): a hidden increase gives one alert with the right N (AC5); three hidden tabs give
  exactly one target (AC6); a visible tab, the same count, or a drop give no alert (AC7); a removed tab is never the target.

  no permission request or alert without a click (AC3); denied → blocked message shown and setting off (AC4);

- The worker wiring is covered by the manual check below rather than an e2e test (e2e tests can't easily cover browser permission prompts across several tabs).

// Decides, once for all tabs sharing the event stream, whether an unread count change deserves a desktop alert.
// No DOM access: it runs inside the shared worker.

export type NotificationTabState = {visible: boolean, count: number};
export type NotificationAlert<Tab> = {tab: Tab, newCount: number};

export class NotificationAlertTracker<Tab> {
  tabs = new Map<Tab, boolean>(); // tab -> visible
  lastVisibleTab: Tab | null = null;
  lastCount: number | null = null;
  baseline = 0; // the count when the user last had Gitea in view, so "new" means new since then

  anyVisible(): boolean {
    for (const visible of this.tabs.values()) {
      if (visible) return true;
    }
    return false;
  }

  setTabState(tab: Tab, {visible, count}: NotificationTabState) {
    this.tabs.set(tab, visible);
    if (this.lastCount === null) {
      this.lastCount = count;
      this.baseline = count;
    }
    if (visible) {
      this.lastVisibleTab = tab;
      this.baseline = this.lastCount;
    }
  }

  removeTab(tab: Tab) {
    this.tabs.delete(tab);
    if (this.lastVisibleTab === tab) this.lastVisibleTab = null;
  }

  onCount(count: number): NotificationAlert<Tab> | null {
    const lastCount = this.lastCount;
    this.lastCount = count;
    if (this.tabs.size === 0) return null;
    if (this.anyVisible()) {
      this.baseline = count;
      return null;
    }
    if (count < this.baseline) this.baseline = count;
    if (lastCount === null || count <= lastCount) return null;
    const tab = this.lastVisibleTab ?? this.tabs.keys().next().value!;
    return {tab, newCount: count - this.baseline};
  }
}

import {isDocumentFragmentOrElementNode} from '../utils/dom.ts';
import type {Promisable} from '../types.ts';
import type {InitPerformanceTracer} from './init.ts';
import {initAriaLabels} from './fomantic/base.ts';

let globalSelectorObserverInited = false;

type SelectorHandler<T extends Element> = {selector: string, handler: (el: T) => void};
const selectorHandlers: SelectorHandler<Element>[] = [];

type GlobalEventFunc<T extends HTMLElement, E extends Event> = (el: T, e: E) => Promisable<void>;
const globalEventFuncs: Record<string, GlobalEventFunc<HTMLElement, Event>> = {};

type GlobalInitFunc<T extends Element> = (el: T) => Promisable<void>;
const globalInitFuncs: Record<string, GlobalInitFunc<Element>> = {};

// It handles the global events for all `<div data-global-click="onSomeElemClick"></div>` elements.
export function registerGlobalEventFunc<T extends HTMLElement, E extends Event>(event: string, name: string, func: GlobalEventFunc<T, E>) {
  globalEventFuncs[`${event}:${name}`] = func as GlobalEventFunc<HTMLElement, Event>;
}

// It handles the global init functions by a selector, for example:
// > registerGlobalSelectorObserver('.ui.dropdown:not(.custom)', (el) => { initDropdown(el, ...) });
// ATTENTION: For most cases, it's recommended to use registerGlobalInitFunc instead,
// Because this selector-based approach is less efficient and less maintainable.
// But if there are already a lot of elements on many pages, this selector-based approach is more convenient for exiting code.
export function registerGlobalSelectorFunc<T extends Element>(selector: string, handler: (el: T) => void) {
  selectorHandlers.push({selector, handler: handler as (el: Element) => void});
  // Then initAddedElementObserver will call this handler for all existing elements after all handlers are added.
  // This approach makes the init stage only need to do one "querySelectorAll".
  if (!globalSelectorObserverInited) return;
  for (const el of document.querySelectorAll<T>(selector)) {
    handler(el);
  }
}

// It handles the global init functions for all `<div data-global-int="initSomeElem"></div>` elements.
export function registerGlobalInitFunc<T extends HTMLElement>(name: string, handler: GlobalInitFunc<T>) {
  globalInitFuncs[name] = handler as GlobalInitFunc<Element>;
  // The "global init" functions are managed internally and called by callGlobalInitFunc
  // They must be ready before initGlobalSelectorObserver is called.
  if (globalSelectorObserverInited) throw new Error('registerGlobalInitFunc() must be called before initGlobalSelectorObserver()');
}

function callGlobalInitFunc(el: Element) {
  // TODO: GLOBAL-INIT-MULTIPLE-FUNCTIONS: maybe in the future we need to extend it to support multiple functions, for example: `data-global-init="func1 func2 func3"`
  const initFunc = el.getAttribute('data-global-init')!;
  const func = globalInitFuncs[initFunc];
  if (!func) throw new Error(`Global init function "${initFunc}" not found`);

  // when an element node is removed and added again, it should not be re-initialized again.
  type GiteaGlobalInitElement = Partial<Element> & {_giteaGlobalInited: boolean};
  if ((el as GiteaGlobalInitElement)._giteaGlobalInited) return;
  (el as GiteaGlobalInitElement)._giteaGlobalInited = true;

  func(el);
}

```typescript
import {localUserSettings} from '../modules/user-settings.ts';
import {registerGlobalInitFunc} from '../modules/observer.ts';
import {trN} from '../modules/i18n.ts';
import {toggleElem} from '../utils/dom.ts';

const {appSubUrl} = window.config;
// stored per browser, because the permission it depends on is per browser too
const desktopAlertsSettingKey = 'notification-desktop-alerts';

function notificationApiAvailable(): boolean {
  return 'Notification' in window;
}

export function desktopAlertsEnabled(): boolean {
  // a permission revoked after opting in reads as off
  return notificationApiAvailable() && Notification.permission === 'granted' && localUserSettings.getBoolean(desktopAlertsSettingKey);
}

export function showDesktopAlert(newCount: number) {
  if (newCount <= 0 || !desktopAlertsEnabled()) return;
  const textEl = document.querySelector('.notification_count')!;
  // only a count, so no private issue or repo names reach a lock screen
  const body = trN(newCount, textEl.getAttribute('data-desktop-alert-1')!, textEl.getAttribute('data-desktop-alert-n')!);
  const icon = document.querySelector<HTMLLinkElement>('link[rel~="icon"]')?.href;
  // the shared tag makes the browser replace an earlier alert instead of stacking one per update or tab
  const alert = new Notification(textEl.getAttribute('data-desktop-alert-title')!, {body, icon, tag: `gitea-notifications:${appSubUrl}`});
  alert.addEventListener('click', () => {
    window.focus();
    window.location.assign(`${appSubUrl}/notifications`);
    alert.close();
  });
}

export function initNotificationDesktopToggle(el: HTMLElement) {
  if (!notificationApiAvailable()) return; // the wrapper stays hidden
  const button = el.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>('.notification-desktop-toggle')!;
  const blocked = el.querySelector('.notification-desktop-blocked')!;

  const render = (showBlocked: boolean) => {
    const enabled = desktopAlertsEnabled();
    toggleElem(el.querySelector('.notification-desktop-enable')!, !enabled);
    toggleElem(el.querySelector('.notification-desktop-disable')!, enabled);
    toggleElem(blocked, showBlocked);
    button.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(enabled));
  };

  button.addEventListener('click', async () => {
    if (desktopAlertsEnabled()) {
      localUserSettings.setBoolean(desktopAlertsSettingKey, false);
      render(false);
      return;
    }
    // browsers only allow the permission prompt from a user click, so this is the one place it is asked
    const permission = Notification.permission === 'default' ? await Notification.requestPermission() : Notification.permission;
    localUserSettings.setBoolean(desktopAlertsSettingKey, permission === 'granted');
    render(permission === 'denied');
  });

  render(Notification.permission === 'denied');
  toggleElem(el, true);
}

export function initNotificationDesktop() {
  registerGlobalInitFunc('initNotificationDesktopToggle', initNotificationDesktopToggle);
}

});

  tracker.setTabState('a', {visible: false, count: 3});
  expect(tracker.onCount(4)).toEqual({tab: 'a', newCount: 1});
});

test('a closed tab is never picked to show the alert', () => {

  tracker.setTabState('a', {visible: true, count: 0});
  tracker.setTabState('b', {visible: false, count: 0});
  tracker.removeTab('a');
  expect(tracker.onCount(1)).toEqual({tab: 'b', newCount: 1});
  tracker.removeTab('b');

```typescript
import {desktopAlertsEnabled, initNotificationDesktopToggle, showDesktopAlert} from './notification-desktop.ts';
import {createElementFromHTML} from '../utils/dom.ts';

class FakeNotification extends EventTarget {
  static permission: NotificationPermission = 'default';
  static requestPermission = vi.fn<() => Promise<NotificationPermission>>();
  static shown: FakeNotification[] = [];
  title: string;
  options: NotificationOptions;
  close = vi.fn();
  constructor(title: string, options: NotificationOptions) {
    super();
    this.title = title;
    this.options = options;
    FakeNotification.shown.push(this);
  }
}

// the navbar count every signed-in page renders, and the toggle notification_div.tmpl renders
function setupPage() {
  document.body.innerHTML = `
    <span class="notification_count" data-desktop-alert-title="Gitea" data-desktop-alert-1="You have %d new notification" data-desktop-alert-n="You have %d new notifications">0</span>`;
  const toggle = createElementFromHTML<HTMLElement>(`
    <div class="tw-hidden">
      <button type="button" class="notification-desktop-toggle">
        <span class="notification-desktop-enable">Enable desktop notifications</span>
        <span class="notification-desktop-disable tw-hidden">Disable desktop notifications</span>
      </button>
      <span class="notification-desktop-blocked tw-hidden">Desktop notifications are blocked by your browser.</span>
    </div>`);
  document.body.append(toggle);
  initNotificationDesktopToggle(toggle);
  const visible = (selector: string) => !toggle.querySelector(selector)!.classList.contains('tw-hidden');
  const button = toggle.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>('.notification-desktop-toggle')!;
  return {toggle, button, visible};
}

// these tests share document.body and the stubbed globals, so they must not run concurrently
describe('desktop notifications', {concurrent: false}, () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    vi.stubGlobal('localStorage', new Storage()); // Node's own localStorage global hides happy-dom's
    FakeNotification.permission = 'default';
    FakeNotification.requestPermission = vi.fn();
    FakeNotification.shown = [];
    vi.stubGlobal('Notification', FakeNotification);
  });
  afterEach(() => {
    vi.restoreAllMocks();
    vi.unstubAllGlobals();
    document.body.innerHTML = '';
  });

  test('AC3 never enabled: no alert and no permission prompt', () => {
    const {toggle, visible} = setupPage();
    showDesktopAlert(1);
    expect(FakeNotification.shown).toHaveLength(0);
    expect(FakeNotification.requestPermission).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(toggle.classList.contains('tw-hidden')).toBe(false);
    expect(visible('.notification-desktop-enable')).toBe(true);
  });

  test('AC3 permission granted for something else does not turn alerts on by itself', () => {
    FakeNotification.permission = 'granted';
    setupPage();
    showDesktopAlert(1);
    expect(FakeNotification.shown).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('AC4 denying the browser prompt says it is blocked and leaves the setting off', async () => {
    FakeNotification.requestPermission.mockResolvedValue('denied');
    const {button, visible} = setupPage();
    button.click();
    await vi.waitFor(() => expect(visible('.notification-desktop-blocked')).toBe(true));
    expect(FakeNotification.requestPermission).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(desktopAlertsEnabled()).toBe(false);
    expect(visible('.notification-desktop-enable')).toBe(true);
  });

  test('allowing the browser prompt turns alerts on', async () => {
    FakeNotification.requestPermission.mockImplementation(() => {
      FakeNotification.permission = 'granted';
      return Promise.resolve('granted');
    });
    const {button, visible} = setupPage();
    button.click();
    await vi.waitFor(() => expect(visible('.notification-desktop-disable')).toBe(true));
    expect(desktopAlertsEnabled()).toBe(true);
    expect(visible('.notification-desktop-blocked')).toBe(false);
  });

  test('AC5 the alert says how many new notifications there are and nothing else', () => {
    FakeNotification.permission = 'granted';
    const {button} = setupPage();
    button.click(); // permission is already granted, so this enables without a prompt
    showDesktopAlert(1);
    showDesktopAlert(3);
    expect(FakeNotification.requestPermission).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(FakeNotification.shown.map((n) => n.options.body)).toEqual(['You have 1 new notification', 'You have 3 new notifications']);
    expect(FakeNotification.shown[0].title).toBe('Gitea');
  });

  test('AC8 clicking the alert focuses Gitea and opens the notifications page', () => {
    FakeNotification.permission = 'granted';
    const {button} = setupPage();
    button.click();
    const focus = vi.spyOn(window, 'focus').mockImplementation(() => {});
    const assign = vi.spyOn(window.location, 'assign').mockImplementation(() => undefined);
    showDesktopAlert(1);
    FakeNotification.shown[0].dispatchEvent(new Event('click'));
    expect(focus).toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(assign).toHaveBeenCalledWith('/notifications');
    expect(FakeNotification.shown[0].close).toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  test('AC9 disabling stops further alerts', async () => {
    FakeNotification.permission = 'granted';
    const {button, visible} = setupPage();
    button.click();
    expect(visible('.notification-desktop-disable')).toBe(true);
    button.click();
    await vi.waitFor(() => expect(visible('.notification-desktop-enable')).toBe(true));
    showDesktopAlert(1);
    expect(FakeNotification.shown).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});

Carson's setup (2026-09-14): **all code edits happen in this Windows `Gitea` folder** (logged
SpecStory sessions launch here). WSL Debian `~/gitea` is a **test runner only** — never edit there.
Native Windows test runs produce Windows-only failures, and lint is ~20x slower, so don't trust them.

**Run tests/lint/build with `wsync` from the Bash tool (Git Bash):**
```bash
wsync pnpm exec vitest run web_src/js/features/common-page.test.ts
wsync go test -run '^TestName$' ./routers/web/misc/
wsync make lint-js
wsync make build
wsync            # sync only
```
`C:\Users\carso\bin\wsync` reads the branch checked out here, warns if tracked files are
uncommitted (only COMMITTED work reaches WSL — commit first, ask Carson before committing), then
runs WSL `~/bin/wsync-wsl <branch> [cmd]`: fetches remote `win` (this folder over /mnt/c;
push disabled), force-switches `~/gitea` to that branch, runs the command with Go 1.26.4/Node PATH.

Gotchas: don't run `git status` on `/mnt/c` from WSL (hangs); WSL can't run `.exe`s; use
`wsl -d Debian --exec bash -c '...' name args` (plain `wsl -- bash -c` drops args).
To try the app: `~/gitea/custom/conf/app.ini` serves Gitea on http://localhost:3001 (SQLite) —
run `wsl -d Debian --exec bash -c 'cd ~/gitea && ./gitea web'` in the background after `wsync make build`.
Baseline rule: some backend tests fail on `main` too — compare branch vs `main`, not vs zero.

I've implemented issue #118 on a new branch, `feat/issue-118-notification-alerts`, off the latest `main`. Nothing is committed yet. The 3 new test files and the existing notification tests pass (29 tests), and eslint and `tsc --noEmit` are clean on the changed files. The template lint and the hands-on browser check haven't been done yet.

**What changed**

- **`modules/favicon-status.ts`:** The tab icon now tracks two badges: an Actions run's status and the unread dot. The run status wins (AC2), and leaving a run page brings the dot back if anything is unread. The dot uses the same `--color-primary` as the navbar's unread bubble. `RepoActionView.vue` didn't need to change.
- **`modules/notification-alert.ts` (new):** A small class with no DOM access that decides whether to alert. It returns no alert when any Gitea tab is visible or the count didn't go up. Otherwise it picks one tab, the one you used last. The number in the alert counts what arrived since you last had Gitea in view, so a second alert replaces the first and covers both.
- **`eventsource.sharedworker.ts` and `modules/worker.ts`:** The worker gets each count update once, asks that class whether to alert, and sends `notification-alert` to that one tab only (AC6/AC7). Each tab tells the worker whether it's visible and what its count is.
- **`features/notification-desktop.ts` (new):** The per-browser on/off setting, stored in `localUserSettings` as Decision 1 says. The browser only asks for permission when you click the button (AC3, AC4). The alert body is the count only (AC5). Clicking the alert focuses Gitea and opens `/notifications` (AC8).
- **`features/notification.ts`:** Both update paths (live updates and the polling fallback) now update the dot. If polling is used, each tab decides for itself, and a shared notification tag makes the browser merge their alerts into one.
- **Templates and locale:** The toggle button and the "blocked" message go next to "Group by repository". Because desktop alerts can appear on any page, their text sits as `data-` attributes on the navbar count. I added 5 keys to `locale_en-US.json` only.

Two things I adjusted while testing:
- In tests, the favicon module remembers the original icon links only once, as it does on a real page, so the test helper reuses the existing links instead of replacing them.
- The tests set `<html lang>` for `trN`, as `repo-issue.test.ts` does, because the test page leaves it empty.

**Tests I wrote, for the PR's Test Evidence section.** I took the expected values from the ACs.
- `web_src/js/modules/favicon-status.test.ts`: added 4 tests (AC1, AC2, dot color). The existing tests are unchanged.
- `web_src/js/modules/notification-alert.test.ts`: new, 6 tests (AC5, AC6, AC7, closed tabs).
- `web_src/js/features/notification-desktop.test.ts`: new, 7 tests (AC3, AC4, AC5, AC8, AC9, enabling).

**Still to run**
1. **Full checks in WSL:** `wsync make lint-js` and `wsync make lint-templates`. `wsync` only sees committed work, so these wait for the commit.
2. **Manual browser check:** the cross-tab path in the worker has no automated test, so it needs two tabs and a second user. Check that the dot appears and clears, that a run page shows its status instead, and walk through enable, deny, allow and disable. Then check that two hidden tabs give exactly one alert, and a visible tab gives none.

If you approve the commit, this is the message I'd use:

```
feat(notifications): badge tab icon and opt-in desktop alerts (#118)

Assisted-by: Claude Code:claude-opus-5-5
```

The trailer is `Assisted-by` only, with no `Co-Authored-By` or `Signed-off-by`, as `AGENTS.md` says. Shall I commit?

Claude in Chrome is a browser extension. Its tools, named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`, act in the person's real Chrome, in new tabs alongside the person's own, with their existing sign-ins. Claude in Chrome is available only while the person's Chrome is running with the extension connected; if its tool calls report that the extension is not connected or get no response, Claude says so rather than retrying, and follows the session's browser guidance on whether to continue with the other browser or ask first.

If the only Claude in Chrome tool present is `enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome`, Claude calls it first: it turns Claude in Chrome on for this conversation, and the `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*` tools appear once it has run.

## Loading the tools

If the `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*` tools are deferred (meaning they have to be loaded through ToolSearch before use), Claude loads every tool it expects to need in ONE ToolSearch call, because the select query accepts a comma-separated list and each extra ToolSearch call costs a full round trip. The core set to start with:

```
ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"
```

Claude adds task-specific tools to that same call when the task obviously needs them: `read_console_messages` and `read_network_requests` for debugging, `form_input` for forms, `gif_creator` for recordings, `javascript_tool` for page scripting. A second ToolSearch is only for a tool the task turned out to need later.

## Starting a session: tab context first, then a new tab

At the start of each browser session Claude calls `mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp` first, to see the person's current tabs and understand what they may want to work with. Then:

1. Claude reuses an existing tab only when the person explicitly asks to work with it.
2. Otherwise Claude opens a new tab with `mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp` and works there, and, unless the person wants them kept, closes the tabs it created before finishing.
3. Claude never reuses tab IDs remembered from an earlier or different session. If a tool reports that a tab does not exist or is invalid, or the person closes a tab, or a navigation error occurs, Claude calls `tabs_context_mcp` again for fresh tab IDs.

## Site permissions

Claude in Chrome acts on a site only once the person has allowed it; depending on their settings the person may be prompted per site, in the extension or in the app. When a tool call is waiting on or refused that permission, Claude tells the person and waits for them to allow it rather than working around it. A site the person declines is their decision; Claude moves on.

## Recording a GIF

For multi-step interactions the person may want to review or share, Claude can record them with `mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator`. Claude captures a few extra frames before and after each action so playback is smooth, and gives the file a meaningful name (for example "login_process.gif").

## Reading console output

`mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages` reads the page's console. Console output can be verbose, so when Claude is looking for specific entries it passes the `pattern` parameter (a regular expression), for example pattern "[MyApp]" to keep only the application's own logs.

## Alerts and dialogs

Claude does not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or other browser modal dialogs through its actions. Those dialogs block all further browser events, so the extension stops receiving commands. Instead:

1. Claude avoids clicking elements likely to raise a confirmation dialog (for example a "Delete" button) unless necessary.
2. If it must interact with such an element, Claude warns the person first that this may interrupt the session.
3. Claude can use `mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool` to check for and dismiss an existing dialog before proceeding, and prefers `console.log` plus `read_console_messages` over `alert` for debugging.

If a dialog does get triggered and the browser stops responding, Claude tells the person they need to dismiss it manually in Chrome.

## Staying on task, and when to stop

Claude stays focused on the specific task and does not wander into unrelated pages. Claude stops and asks the person how to proceed, explaining what it tried and what went wrong, when any of these happen:

- browser tool calls fail or return errors after 2 or 3 attempts
- the extension gives no response
- page elements do not respond to clicks or input, or pages do not load or time out
- the task turns out to involve unexpected complexity or tangents
- several approaches have not completed the task

Claude does not keep retrying the same failing action.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-11 14:54:26Z)**_

Issue #118 passes in a real browser: all 9 ACs plus the polling fallback, with no code changes needed. I tested against the WSL build on `localhost:3001`, using two throwaway accounts: `i118-sender` triggered notifications for `i118-viewer`.

| AC | What happened | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AC1 | The dot appeared live when the count went 0→1, and on a fresh page load with unread notifications. Reading everything restored the default icon without a reload. | ✅ |
| AC2 | The Actions run page kept the run's "waiting" status icon, both on load and while the count went 1→2 live. | ✅ |
| AC3 | Nothing asked for permission until the button was clicked. With permission granted but the setting off, no alert appeared. | ✅ |
| AC4 | After you clicked Block, the page said notifications were blocked and the setting stayed off, also after a reload. | ✅ |
| AC5 | With both tabs hidden: one alert, "You have 1 new notification", with no issue title or repo name. | ✅ |
| AC6 | With two hidden Gitea tabs, exactly one alert, shown by the tab you'd used most recently. | ✅ |
| AC7 | With a tab visible, no alert. With the count dropping 4→0 while hidden, no alert. | ✅ |
| AC8 | Clicking the alert opened `/notifications`. | ✅ |
| AC9 | After Disable, a hidden-tab increase gave no alert. The dot still appeared, as the spec's open question proposed. | ✅ |
| Polling fallback | With the event stream turned off, a hidden tab that polled showed the same count-only alert. | ✅ |

**How much these results prove:**
- **Alert counts:** I counted alerts with a small hook in each tab that recorded every alert and still let Chrome show it. I never saw the actual Windows pop-ups. Did you see "You have 1 new notification" appear?
- **AC8:** I fired the alert's click event rather than clicking the real pop-up. That runs the same code a real click does, so the navigation result holds. The "Gitea got focus" part proves little, because the extension brings tabs forward on its own.
- **Visibility:** Tabs count as visible while the extension is actively using them. So for the hidden-tab tests I let the browser sit idle for 30 s first, and logged each tab's visibility changes to confirm both were hidden when the count changed.
- **Polling, two tabs:** In the polling run, only one tab happened to poll during the window. If two tabs both alert in that mode, Chrome should merge the alerts because they share a tag, but I didn't see that happen.

**Left behind:**
- The test instance's `app.ini` is restored and the server is stopped (it wasn't running before). My browser tabs are closed.
- The test database still has the two `i118-*` accounts and the `alerts-demo` repo. Their generated passwords are in a gitignored file, `~/gitea/custom/test-users-issue118.env`. I can delete all of that if you want.
- Chrome now remembers notifications as **blocked** for `127.0.0.1:3001` and **allowed** for `localhost:3001`. You can reset either from the site-info icon in the address bar.

Next would be pushing the branch and drafting the PR in the course format; the Test Evidence section can include this table. Want me to do that?

# AI assistance disclosure — required format

Course rule, not an upstream Gitea one. Every contributor discloses their own AI use per issue,
**even when no AI was used**. Source: the course AI Log Instructions page and `CONTRIBUTING.md`
(AI Contribution Policy). Two separate places, both required. The rest of the PR and issue
format is in `COURSE-WORKFLOW.md`.

## 1. A comment on the issue

Posted by each contributor on the **issue** they worked, once their work is done. One comment per
person — never edit someone else's. Add later sessions by editing your own table.

```markdown
### AI Assistance — @your-github-username

**Role in this issue:** Implementation

| # | Tool | Log | What AI helped with |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | claude-code | [2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl.md](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/blob/main/ai-logs/sprint1/YourName/2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl.md) | Confirmed the files found during concept location, drafted the template change and tests, ran them |

**Attachments:** [2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl/](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/tree/main/ai-logs/sprint1/YourName/2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl)
```

- **Role** is one of Implementation, Code review, Testing, Other — pick the ones that apply and
  delete the rest, do not leave the slash list in place.
- **Tool** is the tool's name, e.g. `claude-code`, `claude-web`.
- **Log** is a full `https://github.com/...` link to the filed log. Relative paths break in issue
  comments. File naming is in `ai-logs/README.md`.
- **Attachments** only when the log has a companion folder; otherwise drop the line.
- **No AI used?** Keep the heading and role line and write `No AI used` in place of the table.

## 2. A short section in the pull request description — no log link

Reviewers read the PR, and the review rubric scores "AI transparency", so the PR says how AI was
used and how you verified it. It does **not** link or cite the AI log: from Sprint 1 on, the team
references logs in **issue comments only**, never in PR descriptions or PR comments (Sprint 1 page,
D5; later sprint pages also accept the PR, and the issue comment satisfies both).

```markdown
## AI assistance

Claude Code (claude-opus-5) drafted the handler and tests following the existing register/delete
code; I reviewed every line, ran the tests, checked the page by hand, and can explain each change.
AI log: see the AI Assistance comment on the linked issue.
```

Name the model, say what AI did and what you did, and point at the issue comment for the log. The
PR's Test Evidence section has its own **AI-written tests** line, which names the tests AI wrote or
changed and how you checked their expected values (`COURSE-WORKFLOW.md`, "Pull request format").

## Rules that make a disclosure wrong

- **Placeholders left in**: `@your-github-username` or the full `Implementation / Code review /
  Testing / Other` list means the comment was pasted unread.
- **A log link in a PR description or PR comment.** Log links live in the issue comment only.
- **A log link that 404s.** Until the log is merged to `main`, link the branch that holds it; switch
  to the `main` link once merged.
- **A log folder that is not your GitHub username** — `ai-logs/sprint1/jdonohue/` is wrong when the
  account is `Jack-Donohue`.
- **Claiming work AI did as your own, or the reverse.** The claim must match the log.
- **AI-written replies to reviewer questions on your own issue or PR.** `CONTRIBUTING.md` forbids it:
  the questions are for you.

## For AI agents drafting an issue or PR

Put section 2 in every PR description you draft, and draft the section 1 issue comment
separately, both filled in from the session you actually ran — never with placeholders. You may
draft the wording, but say plainly that the human must review and edit it before posting, and leave
the issue comment for them to post under their own account.
```
</details></tool-use>

### Graded strictly this sprint

The Sprint 3 page lists these as the rules that cost the most points. Details are in the sections
named.

1. No merge without a teammate's approval on the PR's **latest commit** (Reviews, below).
2. A spec review comment on the issue that says what was checked (Spec review, under the issue

3. Every code PR has `Closes #<N>`, and both the issue and the PR are on the `Sprint 3` milestone.
4. Real AI logs, linked from the issue (D5).
5. A Test Evidence table in every PR, with expected values not copied from the code's output
   (Pull request format).
6. Mutation testing with a tool, with before and after reports committed (Mutation testing (D6)).
7. The team introduces no new test failures. A skipped test or a disabled CI check needs a linked
   issue and a reason in a code comment (D8).

### Deliverable notes
