## Branches and commits

- Branches: `feat/issue-<N>-short-description`, `fix/issue-<N>-short-description` or
  `chore/short-description` (`STUDENTS.md`). One issue per branch.
- Commit messages follow Conventional Commits and end with the issue number:
  `feat(repo): show empty state on releases page (#17)`. Add an
  `Assisted-by: AGENT_NAME:MODEL_VERSION` trailer when AI helped; never `Co-Authored-By` or
  `Signed-off-by` (`AGENTS.md`). A human approves every commit before it is made.

### Before each implementation: sync with main

Every new branch starts from an up-to-date `main`. AI sessions run this before writing any code:

```bash
git switch main
git pull origin main
git switch -c feat/issue-<N>-short-description
```

To pick up new work on `main` for a branch that already exists, **merge, don't rebase**. Rebasing
or squashing after review has started is not allowed (`docs/sprint0/standards.md`):

```bash
git fetch origin
git merge origin/main
```

Do this before opening the PR and again if `main` moves while it is in review. A merge pushed after
approval needs a new approval (see Reviews). Never merge another feature branch into yours.

....
## Pull request format

Template: `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Title uses Conventional Commits, e.g.
`fix(issues): keep label filter after search`. Description sections:

1. `Closes #<N>`, which links the issue and closes it on merge. Every code PR links its issue, and
   the PR goes on the `Sprint 3` milestone too.
2. **What changed:** the change in your own words.
3. **Why:** the problem, and which acceptance criteria (AC1…) it satisfies.
4. **Test Evidence:** required from Sprint 3. It replaces the old "How it was tested" section.
   Every behaviour change still needs a new or updated test.

   ```markdown
   ## Test Evidence

   | Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | AC1: ... | ... | ... | ... |

   **Not tested automatically, and why:** [...]

   **AI-written tests:** [Which tests were written or modified by AI, and how you checked that their expected values are correct. If none, write "None."]
   ```

   - **One row per acceptance criterion** from the issue; for a bug report, the Expected Behavior.
     A PR that changes no product behaviour (e.g. a CI change) writes `N/A` and why.
   - **Test(s):** the test name, plus the file if not obvious. For a manual check, write `Manual:`
     followed by the steps and what you saw. An AC tested both ways lists both in the same row.
   - **Level:** `unit`, `integration`, `E2E` or `manual`.
   - **Source of expected value:** `AC`, `issue discussion`, `docs`, `upstream behavior`, or
     `other` (explain). **Never the current output of your own code:** a test whose expected value
     was copied from what the code returns cannot detect that the code is wrong.
   - **Not tested automatically, and why:** only for ACs checked manually only.
   - AI may draft this section; the author checks that it is accurate.

5. **CI / manual verification:** CI status. If CI doesn't run your tests, the commands you ran and
   a summary of the results (passed, failed, skipped).
6. **Design:** one line pointing at the Design Decision in the issue, or a note on how it changed.
7. **Tech Debt:** required from Sprint 2. Both fields are required, and `None.` is a valid answer:

   ```markdown
   ## Tech Debt

   **Introduced:** <shortcuts, workarounds or design compromises this PR makes, and why>

   **Encountered:** <tech debt that was already there and that you ran into, and how you handled it>
   ```

8. **AI assistance:** format in `AI-ASSISTANCE.md` §2, with **no log link**.

Per-PR grading (20 points): correctness against the acceptance criteria 6; tests written or updated
appropriately, with the Test Evidence section complete, every AC covered and expected values
justified 6; description explains what and why, Tech Debt section present, issue linked 3; CI passes
or manual verification documented 3; reviewed with the rubric (including the test evidence row),
reviewer comment posted, merged only after an approval on the latest commit 2.
```

Closes #118

## What changed

- **Tab icon badge.** `favicon-status.ts` now knows about two badges that can own the tab icon: an Actions run's status and a new unread-notification dot. A single `renderFavicon()` picks one (run status first, then the dot, then the default icon). The dot reuses the run badge's position and white ring, and is filled with `--color-primary` so it matches the navbar's unread bubble. `RepoActionView.vue` is unchanged.
- **Desktop notification opt-in.** A new **Enable desktop notifications** button on the Notifications page (`notification_div.tmpl`, wired in `features/notification-desktop.ts`). The choice is stored per browser in `localUserSettings`. The browser's permission prompt is only requested from that click, and a denial shows "Desktop notifications are blocked by your browser." Clicking it again disables alerts.
- **One alert across tabs.** Every Gitea tab already shares one event stream through `eventsource.sharedworker.ts`. Tabs now tell the worker whether they are visible and what their count is. When the count goes up and no Gitea tab is visible, the worker asks exactly one tab (the one used most recently) to show the alert. The decision logic is a small DOM-free class in `modules/notification-alert.ts` so it can be unit tested.
- **Alert content.** Only a count ("You have N new notification(s)", counting since Gitea was last in view); clicking it focuses Gitea and opens `/notifications`. The text reaches every page as `data-` attributes on the navbar count.
- **Polling fallback.** When the shared worker or event stream is unavailable, a hidden tab that sees the count go up alerts on its own; all alerts share one notification tag so the browser shows one.
- New locale keys in `locale_en-US.json` only.

## Why

Users who leave Gitea in a background tab don't notice review requests and mentions until they switch back. This adds a passive badge (AC1, AC2) and opt-in, count-only desktop alerts that never prompt on their own, fire once across tabs and only when Gitea isn't visible (AC3–AC9).

## Test Evidence

| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AC1: badge dot while unread, default icon back at 0 without a reload | `favicon-status.test.ts`: "AC1 unread notifications add a dot and reading them all restores the default icon"; "the dot uses the primary color". Manual: new notification took the count 0→1 live and both favicon links got the dot; marking all read took it to 0 and restored `favicon.svg`/`favicon.png` with no navigation; loading a repo page with 1 unread showed the dot on load | unit, manual | AC; Decision 3 (dot, same color as navbar badge) |
| AC2: run status wins over the badge on an Actions run page | `favicon-status.test.ts`: "AC2 an Actions run status wins over the dot, and the dot returns when the run page is left"; "AC2 leaving a run page with nothing unread restores the default icon". Manual: on a waiting run with 1 unread the icon showed `waiting`, and it stayed `waiting` when the count rose to 2 live | unit, manual | AC; Decision 3 |
| AC3: never enabled → no alert, no prompt on its own | `notification-desktop.test.ts`: "AC3 never enabled: no alert and no permission prompt"; "AC3 permission granted for something else does not turn alerts on by itself". Manual: permission stayed `default` until the button was clicked | unit, manual | AC; Decision 1 (alternative b rejected) |
| AC4: denied → page says blocked, setting stays off | `notification-desktop.test.ts`: "AC4 denying the browser prompt says it is blocked and leaves the setting off". Manual: clicked Enable, blocked Chrome's prompt; blocked message shown, setting `false`, still shown after reload | unit, manual | AC |
| AC5: hidden tab, count up → one count-only alert | `notification-alert.test.ts`: "AC5 a count increase while every tab is hidden alerts once…"; `notification-desktop.test.ts`: "AC5 the alert says how many new notifications there are and nothing else". Manual: both tabs hidden, 3→4 gave one alert, body "You have 1 new notification" | unit, manual | AC; Decision 2 |
| AC6: several tabs → one alert | `notification-alert.test.ts`: "AC6 several hidden tabs get one alert, sent to the tab used last". Manual: two hidden Gitea tabs, one alert in total, from the tab used last | unit, manual | AC |
| AC7: visible tab, same or lower count → no alert | `notification-alert.test.ts`: "AC7 no alert while any Gitea tab is visible"; "AC7 no alert when the count stays the same or goes down". Manual: count rose while tabs were visible, no alert; count fell 4→0 while hidden, no alert | unit, manual | AC |
| AC8: clicking the alert focuses Gitea and opens `/notifications` | `notification-desktop.test.ts`: "AC8 clicking the alert focuses Gitea and opens the notifications page". Manual: dispatched the alert's click event; the tab moved from the issues list to `/notifications` | unit, manual | AC |
| AC9: disable → no more alerts | `notification-desktop.test.ts`: "AC9 disabling stops further alerts". Manual: clicked Disable (permission still granted), hidden count rise gave no alert | unit, manual | AC |

Also checked manually: with `EVENT_SOURCE_UPDATE_TIME = -1` (polling fallback), a hidden tab that polled showed the same count-only alert (issue's Open Question 2).

**Not tested automatically, and why:** the shared-worker wiring (tabs reporting visibility, the worker routing `notification-alert` to one tab) has no automated test: it needs real browser tabs with real visibility, and an E2E test would need permission grants across several tabs. Its decision logic is unit tested in `notification-alert.test.ts`, and the wiring was checked manually for AC5–AC7 and AC9 above. Manual counts were taken by wrapping `window.Notification` in each tab to record every alert created.

**AI-written tests:** all tests above were written by Claude Code: the four new tests in `web_src/js/modules/favicon-status.test.ts`, and the new files `web_src/js/modules/notification-alert.test.ts` and `web_src/js/features/notification-desktop.test.ts`. Expected values come from the issue's ACs and Design Decisions (dot color, run status precedence, count-only text, per-browser opt-in), not from running the code. I checked each assertion against the AC it names.

## CI / manual verification

- `make lint-js` (eslint + vue-tsc): passed

Manual browser checks against a local build (`make build`, SQLite) are in the Test Evidence table.

## Design

Follows the three Design Decisions in #118: per-browser opt-in in local storage, count-only alerts, and a dot badge where Actions run status takes precedence. Added during implementation: the shared worker decides which tab alerts, so a visible Gitea tab suppresses alerts from hidden ones.

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:** The polling fallback can't coordinate tabs, so two hidden tabs that both detect an increase each create an alert. They share a notification tag, so the browser shows one, but a visible tab in the same browser doesn't suppress them. The shared-worker path only has manual test coverage.

**Encountered:** `UserEventsSharedWorker` closes its port on `beforeunload`, which can be cancelled (existing FIXME in `modules/worker.ts`). A tab whose unload is cancelled may stop reporting to the worker. Left as is, since it predates this change and also affects the stopwatch. The worker class also had no way to send a message without reaching into `sharedWorker.port`; I added a small `postMessage` method.

## Issue #118 spec
ACs:
- **AC1:** Dot on the tab icon when unread > 0; the default icon returns without a reload when the count reaches 0.
- **AC2:** On an Actions run page, the run status icon wins over the dot.
- **AC3:** No alert and no permission prompt unless enabled via a click.
- **AC4:** If the user denies the prompt, the page says notifications are blocked and the setting stays off.
- **AC5:** When the tab is hidden and the count goes up, exactly one count-only alert.
- **AC6:** One alert across several tabs.
- **AC7:** No alert if a tab is visible or the count stays the same or goes down.
- **AC8:** Clicking the alert focuses Gitea and opens `/notifications`.
- **AC9:** Disable stops alerts.

Design decisions:
- **D1:** The opt-in is stored per browser in localStorage.
- **D2:** Count only ("You have N new notifications").
- **D3:** Dot badge, reusing the Actions favicon drawing code; run status takes precedence.

Choices the user made via AskUserQuestion:
- **Cross-tab coordination:** in the shared worker.
- **Dot color:** primary (`--color-primary`, matching the navbar badge).

## Implementation
Branch `feat/issue-118-notification-alerts`, created off origin/main at `2d9f5ae1c7`. Commit `b3fdf8d54f`, message "feat(notifications): badge tab icon and opt-in desktop alerts (#118)" with trailer `Assisted-by: Claude Code:claude-opus-5-5`. 13 files, +446/-12.

### `web_src/js/modules/favicon-status.ts`
- Replaced `currentStatus` with `actionStatus`, `notificationDot`, and `notificationDotDataUrl`.
- Added `buildNotificationFaviconSvg()`: a white ring plus a circle carrying `data-notification-dot`, colored from `--color-primary` with fallback `#4183c4`.
- Added `buildNotificationFaviconDataUrl()` (cached) and `restoreDefaultFavicon()`.
- Added `renderFavicon()`: action status first, then the dot, then the default icon.
- `syncActionRunFavicon` and `resetActionFavicon` keep their signatures and now call `renderFavicon`.
- New export `syncNotificationFaviconDot(show)`.

### `web_src/js/modules/notification-alert.ts` (new)
`NotificationAlertTracker<Tab>` with:
- Fields: `tabs` (Map of tab to visible), `lastVisibleTab`, `lastCount`, `baseline`.
- `anyVisible()` and `removeTab()`.
- `setTabState(tab, {visible, count})`: the first state seeds the count and baseline; a visible tab sets the baseline.
- `onCount(count)`: returns `{tab, newCount: count - baseline}` only when no tab is visible and the count increased. The target is the last visible tab, or else the first tab.

### `web_src/js/eventsource.sharedworker.ts`
- Imports the tracker; `Source.alertTracker` field.
- `listen()` calls `alertNotificationCount(data)` for `notification-count` events and posts `{type:'notification-alert', count}` to one port.
- `deregister` calls `removeTab`.
- New port message `notification-tab-state` is passed to `setTabState`.

### `web_src/js/modules/worker.ts`
Added a `postMessage(message)` method on `UserEventsSharedWorker`.

### `web_src/js/features/notification-desktop.ts` (new)
- Setting key `notification-desktop-alerts` in `localUserSettings`.
- `desktopAlertsEnabled()`: requires the Notification API, permission `granted`, and the setting on.
- `showDesktopAlert(newCount)`: builds the text with `trN` from `data-desktop-alert-1/-n` and the title from `data-desktop-alert-title` on `.notification_count`. Uses tag `gitea-notifications:${appSubUrl}`. Its click handler calls `window.focus()`, `location.assign(appSubUrl + '/notifications')`, then `close()`.
- `initNotificationDesktopToggle(el)`:
  - The button toggles the setting. `requestPermission` is called only in the click handler, and only when permission is `default`.
  - A `.notification-desktop-blocked` message is shown when permission is denied.
  - Sets `aria-pressed`.
- `initNotificationDesktop()` registers the global init `initNotificationDesktopToggle`, and is added to `web_src/js/index.ts` after `initNotificationBulk`.

### `web_src/js/features/notification.ts`
- Calls `syncNotificationFaviconDot` on init, in `receiveUpdateCount`, and in `updateNotificationCount`.
- The shared-worker path posts `notification-tab-state` (visibility and count) at start and on `visibilitychange`, and handles `notification-alert` by calling `showDesktopAlert`.
- In the poll path, `updateNotificationCountWithCallback` alerts with the delta when the count increased and the tab is hidden.

### Templates and locale
- `templates/base/head_navbar_icons.tmpl`: `data-desktop-alert-title="{{AppName}}"`, `data-desktop-alert-1` and `data-desktop-alert-n` on the `.notification_count` span.
- `templates/user/notification/notification_div.tmpl`: after "Group by repository", a `div.flex-text-inline.tw-hidden` with `data-global-init="initNotificationDesktopToggle"`. It holds a button `.notification-desktop-toggle` (with `data-test-id`) containing enable/disable spans, plus a blocked span with `role="status"`.
- `options/locale/locale_en-US.json`: added `notification.desktop_enable`, `desktop_disable`, `desktop_blocked`, `desktop_alert_1` ("You have %d new notification") and `desktop_alert_n`.

### Tests (all AI-written)
- **`favicon-status.test.ts`:** 4 tests added in a `concurrent:false` describe. The helper reuses existing links, because the module remembers its link elements once.
- **`notification-alert.test.ts` (new):** 6 tests.
- **`notification-desktop.test.ts` (new):** 7 tests with a `FakeNotification` stub and a `Storage` stub. `document.documentElement.lang='en-US'` is set because `trN` failed with "RangeError: Invalid language tag:". Uses `replaceChildren()` per eslint `unicorn/prefer-dom-node-replace-children`.

    14	      count.classList.toggle('tw-hidden', data.Count === 0);
    15	      count.textContent = String(data.Count);
    16	    }
    17	    syncNotificationFaviconDot(data.Count > 0);
    18	    await updateNotificationTable();
    19	  } catch (error) {
    20	    console.error(error, event);
    21	  }
    22	}
    23	
    24	export function initNotificationCount() {
    25	  if (!document.querySelector('.notification_count')) return;
    26	  syncNotificationFaviconDot(getCurrentCount() > 0);
    27	
    28	  let usingPeriodicPoller = false;
    29	  const startPeriodicPoller = (timeout: number, lastCount?: number) => {
    30	    if (timeout <= 0 || !Number.isFinite(timeout)) return;
    31	    usingPeriodicPoller = true;
    32	    lastCount = lastCount ?? getCurrentCount();
    33	    setTimeout(async () => {
    34	      await updateNotificationCountWithCallback(startPeriodicPoller, timeout, lastCount);
    35	    }, timeout);
    36	  };
    37	
    38	  if (notificationSettings.EventSourceUpdateTime > 0 && window.EventSource && window.SharedWorker) {
    39	    // Try to connect to the event source via the shared worker first
    40	    const worker = new UserEventsSharedWorker('notification-worker');
    41	    worker.addMessageEventListener((event: MessageEvent) => {
    42	      if (event.data.type === 'no-event-source') {
    43	        if (!usingPeriodicPoller) startPeriodicPoller(notificationSettings.MinTimeout);
    44	      } else if (event.data.type === 'notification-count') {
    45	        receiveUpdateCount(event); // no await
    46	      } else if (event.data.type === 'notification-alert') {
    47	        showDesktopAlert(event.data.count); // the worker picks one tab, so tabs don't each alert
    48	      }
    49	    });
    50	    worker.startPort();
    51	    const postTabState = () => {
    52	      worker.postMessage({type: 'notification-tab-state', visible: document.visibilityState === 'visible', count: getCurrentCount()});
    53	    };
    54	    postTabState();
    55	    document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', postTabState);
    56	    return;
    57	  }
    58	
    59	  startPeriodicPoller(notificationSettings.MinTimeout);
    60	}
    61	
    62	function getCurrentCount() {
    63	  return Number(document.querySelector('.notification_count')!.textContent ?? '0');
    64	}
    65	
    66	async function updateNotificationCountWithCallback(callback: (timeout: number, newCount: number) => void, timeout: number, lastCount: number) {
    67	  const currentCount = getCurrentCount();
    68	  if (lastCount !== currentCount) {
    69	    callback(notificationSettings.MinTimeout, currentCount);
    70	    return;
    71	  }
    72	
    73	  const newCount = await updateNotificationCount();
    74	  let needsUpdate = false;
    75	
    76	  if (lastCount !== newCount) {
    77	    needsUpdate = true;
    78	    // without the shared worker, tabs can't agree on who alerts; the notification tag merges their alerts into one
    79	    if (newCount > lastCount && document.visibilityState === 'hidden') showDesktopAlert(newCount - lastCount);
    80	    timeout = notificationSettings.MinTimeout;
    81	  } else if (timeout < notificationSettings.MaxTimeout) {
    82	    timeout += notificationSettings.TimeoutStep;
    83	  }
    84	
    85	  callback(timeout, newCount);
    86	  if (needsUpdate) {
    87	    await updateNotificationTable();
    88	  }
    89	}
    90	
    91	async function updateNotificationTable() {
    92	  const notificationDiv = document.querySelector('#notification_div');
    93	  if (!notificationDiv) return;
    94	
    95	  try {
    96	    const params = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search);
    97	    params.set('div-only', 'true');
    98	    params.set('sequence-number', String(++notificationSequenceNumber));
    99	    const response = await GET(`${appSubUrl}/notifications?${params.toString()}`);
   100	
   101	    if (!response.ok) {
   102	      throw new Error('Failed to fetch notification table');
   103	    }
   104	
   105	    const data = await response.text();
   106	    const el = createElementFromHTML(data);
   107	    if (parseInt(el.getAttribute('data-sequence-number')!) === notificationSequenceNumber) {
   108	      const flash = notificationDiv.querySelector('.flash-message');
   109	      notificationDiv.outerHTML = data;
   110	      // the page load already consumed the flash, so the refreshed list would drop e.g. a bulk action's confirmation
   111	      const container = document.querySelector('#notification_div > .ui.container')!;
   112	      if (flash && !container.querySelector('.flash-message')) container.prepend(flash);
   113	    }
   114	  } catch (error) {

   116	  }
   117	}

   119	async function updateNotificationCount(): Promise<number> {

   134	    }

/* eslint-disable no-restricted-globals */
// Some people deploy Gitea under a subpath, so it needs prefix to avoid local storage key conflicts.
// And these keys are for user settings only, it also needs a specific prefix,
// in case in the future there are other uses of local storage, and/or we need to clear some keys when the quota is exceeded.
const itemKeyPrefix = 'gitea:setting:';

function handleLocalStorageError(e: any) {
  // in the future, maybe we need to handle quota exceeded errors differently
  console.error('Error using local storage for user settings', e);
}

function getLocalStorageUserSetting(settingKey: string): string | null {
  const legacyKey = settingKey;
  const itemKey = `${itemKeyPrefix}${settingKey}`;
  try {
    const legacyValue = localStorage?.getItem(legacyKey) ?? null;
    const value = localStorage?.getItem(itemKey) ?? null; // avoid undefined
    if (value !== null && legacyValue !== null) {
      // if both values exist, remove the legacy one
      localStorage?.removeItem(legacyKey);
    } else if (value === null && legacyValue !== null) {
      // migrate legacy value to new key
      localStorage?.removeItem(legacyKey);
      localStorage?.setItem(itemKey, legacyValue);
      return legacyValue;
    }
    return value;
  } catch (e) {
    handleLocalStorageError(e);
  }
  return null;
}

function setLocalStorageUserSetting(settingKey: string, value: string) {
  const legacyKey = settingKey;
  const itemKey = `${itemKeyPrefix}${settingKey}`;
  try {
    localStorage?.removeItem(legacyKey);
    localStorage?.setItem(itemKey, value);
  } catch (e) {

const pollEvery = 1000;

// /notifications/new answers with these unread counts, one per poll
function serveCounts(...counts: number[]) {
  for (const count of counts) {
    vi.mocked(GET).mockResolvedValueOnce({ok: true, json: () => Promise.resolve({new: count})} as Response);
  }
}

function setVisibility(state: DocumentVisibilityState) {

describe('notification count poller', {concurrent: false}, () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    vi.useFakeTimers();
    document.documentElement.lang = 'en-US'; // trN resolves plural rules from the document language
    document.body.innerHTML = `

    FakeNotification.shown = [];
    vi.stubGlobal('Notification', FakeNotification);
    localUserSettings.setBoolean('notification-desktop-alerts', true);
    // EventSourceUpdateTime stays 0, so initNotificationCount takes the poller path
    Object.assign(window.config.notificationSettings, {MinTimeout: pollEvery, TimeoutStep: pollEvery, MaxTimeout: pollEvery});
  });
  afterEach(() => {
    vi.clearAllTimers();
    vi.useRealTimers();
    vi.restoreAllMocks();
    vi.mocked(GET).mockReset();
    vi.unstubAllGlobals();
    Object.assign(window.config.notificationSettings, {MinTimeout: 0, TimeoutStep: 0, MaxTimeout: 0});
    document.body.replaceChildren();
  });

  test('AC5 a hidden tab alerts with the number of new notifications since its last poll', async () => {
    setVisibility('hidden');

### Graded strictly this sprint

The Sprint 3 page lists these as the rules that cost the most points. Details are in the sections
named.

1. No merge without a teammate's approval on the PR's **latest commit** (Reviews, below).
2. A spec review comment on the issue that says what was checked (Spec review, under the issue
   formats).
3. Every code PR has `Closes #<N>`, and both the issue and the PR are on the `Sprint 3` milestone.
4. Real AI logs, linked from the issue (D5).
5. A Test Evidence table in every PR, with expected values not copied from the code's output
   (Pull request format).
6. Mutation testing with a tool, with before and after reports committed (Mutation testing (D6)).
7. The team introduces no new test failures. A skipped test or a disabled CI check needs a linked
   issue and a reason in a code comment (D8).
8. A sprint report that renders on GitHub and uses the Sprint 3 sections (D8).

### Deliverable notes

- **D1 load:** each CSCI 435 student owns at least 2 medium issues; each CSCI 535 student owns at
  least 2 medium and 1 small. Either load can be met with equivalent story points instead. Every
  issue has exactly **one** assignee. Unfinished Sprint 2 issues go into the backlog before new
  work. To drop one, write the reason on that issue. If the backlog is too thin to meet the load,
  find areas that still need work (features, improvements, test gaps, bugs) and write new issues
The site doesn't say where the evidence goes: plan it in the issue (Evidence of Fix, or Additional
Information for a bug), then post the results on the issue and in the PR's Test Evidence once the
fix is in. Regenerating snapshots, reformatting code, or silencing a check without fixing its cause
counts as small at most.

### Design Decision and spec review

- **Design Decision (D3):** fill it in once you've picked an approach, before opening the PR. Put
  a second decision under another `### Decision 2` heading. If a PR changes the decision, update
  the issue body.
- **Spec review (D2):** before coding starts, a teammate posts a review comment **on the issue**.
  Start it with `Spec reviewed` so it is easy to find. The layout is the reviewer's choice, but the
  comment must say what was checked:
  1. each acceptance criterion: clear and testable, naming any that aren't;
  2. the cases considered (e.g. empty input, errors, permissions) and whether the ACs cover them;
  3. whether the scope fits the stated size;

  and end with an approval, or the problems for the author to fix in the spec. `Looks good!` with
  nothing about what was checked does not count. An optional layout:

  ```markdown
  Spec reviewed — @reviewer-username

  **Acceptance criteria:** <clear and testable? which aren't, and why>
  **Cases considered:** <which cases, and whether the ACs cover them>
  **Scope:** <does it fit the stated size?>
  **Verdict:** Approved | Changes needed: <list>
  ```

## Pull request format

35:Reviewers read the PR, and the review rubric scores "AI transparency", so the PR says how AI was
62:- **AI-written replies to reviewer questions on your own issue or PR.** `CONTRIBUTING.md` forbids it:
---
name: gitea-ai-usage-guardrail
description: Standing instruction - flag Gitea-repo requests that risk grade/Honor Code trouble, only for that project
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Carson asked 2026-09-03: for [[csci-435-gitea-project]] specifically, before doing something he
asks (or before handing him ready-to-use text/code), check it against [[gitea-ai-honor-code-rules]].
If a request would likely cross one of those lines, say so briefly and either propose a safer
rephrasing or let him decide - don't just silently comply, and don't refuse outright either (these
are grading-process risks, not something to gatekeep hard on).

**Concretely, flag rather than silently doing it when asked to, e.g.:**
- Write a PR description, issue reply, or reviewer-question answer that reads as final/ready to
  post verbatim, with no prompt to review or edit it first.
- Implement an issue Carson opened himself (should be someone else's, per D5).
- Skip straight to using AI to locate/understand code for an issue before he's looked himself
  (concept location must come first).
- Skip or postpone AI-log capture for a session doing real project work.
- Draft an "AI Assistance" issue/PR comment that mischaracterizes what AI did (or skip posting one).
- Anything implying shared account access with a teammate.

**Why:** Syllabus §16 makes "prompt → copy → paste" without review an Honor Code violation, and
several Sprint 0 D5 rules (concept-location-first, must-explain-every-line, no AI replies on your
own issue/PR) are graded process, not just suggestions. Carson wants a heads-up before he
accidentally does something in that gray zone, not after.

**How to apply:** Scope this to Gitea/CSCI 435 work ONLY - do not extend this caution to his other
coursework or general use, and don't be preachy about it: one short flag + an alternative or a

=================== #154
S1. Render `suggestion` blocks in review comments as a diff by vvchopra 2026-11-11T01:46:01Z

### User Story

Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: medium` · Type: Feature · Part of #151

## User Story
As a PR author, I want a reviewer's suggested code to show as a before/after diff in the review
comment so that I can see exactly what would change without comparing it to the file myself.

### User Scenario

## User Scenario
Ana reviews PR #42. On line 18 of `main.go` she writes a code comment containing

````markdown
```suggestion
	return fmt.Errorf("open %s: %w", name, err)
```
````

and submits the review. Ben, the author, opens the Conversation tab. Under Ana's comment he sees
a small diff: line 18 as it is now in red, her replacement in green, labelled "Suggested change".
The same rendering appears on the Files changed tab. Text outside the block renders as normal
markdown.


### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given a code comment on a new-side line whose body has one ```` ```suggestion ```` block,
  when the comment is shown in the Conversation or Files changed tab, then the block renders as a
  diff headed "Suggested change": the commented line as removed (red) and each line of the block
  as added (green), with indentation kept.
- [ ] AC2: Given an empty ```` ```suggestion ```` block, when rendered, then it shows the commented
  line as removed and nothing added (a "delete this line" suggestion).
- [ ] AC3: Given a ```` ```suggestion ```` block in a plain issue or PR comment (not a code
  comment), when rendered, then it shows as an ordinary code block, not a diff.
- [ ] AC4: Given a code comment with two or more suggestion blocks, when rendered, then each block
  renders as its own diff against the same commented line. (S3 decides whether to offer Apply.)
- [ ] AC5: Given suggestion content containing HTML such as `<script>alert(1)</script>`, when
  rendered, then it is shown as literal text and nothing is executed.
- [ ] AC6: Given an outdated code comment (the branch moved and the comment is `Invalidated`), when
  rendered, then the diff is still shown against the line the reviewer originally commented on,
  next to the existing "Outdated" label.
- [ ] AC7: Given a code comment on an old-side (deleted) line, or one whose stored diff context is
  missing, when rendered, then the suggestion block shows as an ordinary code block and the page
  has no errors.
- [ ] AC8: Given a code comment with a suggestion is edited, when the edit is saved, then the
  updated block renders as a diff without reloading the page.

### Out of Scope

- Applying the suggestion (S3); multi-line ranges (S5); the editor button (S2).
- Suggestions in commit comments outside a PR (#151 out of scope).
- Suggestions on old-side (deleted) lines, until the customer answers question 5 on #151.
- Syntax highlighting inside the suggestion diff.

### Open Questions

- Should the old side of the diff come from the comment's stored diff context (what the reviewer
  saw) or from the file at the current head? (Decided: stored context, so the diff never changes
  under the reader; S3 does the "has it changed since" check.)
- Old-side suggestions: waiting on customer question 5 on #151.


### Design Decision

**Decision:** Render the diff in the browser, the same way Gitea already renders `mermaid` and
`math` code blocks. The server takes the commented line from the comment's stored diff context
(`Comment.Patch`, whose last line is always the commented line) through a new
`Comment.SuggestionOriginalLine()` method, and puts it in a `data-suggestion-original` attribute
on the body of new-side code comments only. A new `web_src/js/markup/suggestion.ts`, registered
beside the mermaid and math handlers, replaces each `code.language-suggestion` block inside such a
body with a diff, building it with `textContent` only.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Post-process the rendered HTML on the server.* After markdown renders a code comment, Go would
  find the `<pre><code class="language-suggestion">` and swap in a template-rendered diff. It works
  without JavaScript, but it rewrites already-sanitised HTML and has to be repeated in both places
  that render code comments (the page load and the edit-comment save).
- *A markdown renderer extension in `modules/markup`.* The renderer would emit the diff directly,
  but it would need to know which file and line a comment belongs to, which it doesn't carry for
  any other content, and the sanitiser's allowlist would need new classes.

**Rationale:** It follows an existing pattern (mermaid, math), leaves the markdown renderer and
sanitiser untouched, and the attribute on new-side code comments only is what keeps plain comments
as plain code blocks (AC3). Editing a comment re-runs the same frontend hook, so AC8 needs no
extra server code.

**Consequences:** Without JavaScript a suggestion shows as a plain code block. S3 and S7 must find
suggestion blocks in Go themselves (using goldmark's parser, so they agree with what the page
shows); S1 gives them `SuggestionOriginalLine()` to compare against.

### Scope

medium

### Scope Justification

Medium scope because it touches a good amount of components in the code
--- comments

(XSS, outdated, missing context) are good. AC2 should say whether a fence with one blank line
counts as "empty" (delete the line) or replaces the line with a blank. AC7's "no errors" should
be observable, e.g. "no console errors".

**Cases considered:** Main path, empty block, several blocks, plain comment, XSS, outdated,
old-side line and edit-without-reload are all covered. Missing:
- replies in a code-comment thread (add to AC1)
- the review summary body, which should behave like AC3
- which fence variants count (`~~~suggestion`, `Suggestion`), so S3/S7 parse the same blocks

**Scope:** Medium fits (a model method, a template attribute, a new frontend handler, tests). But
the justification needs to name the components and the expected size of change, not just "a

2. Add the missing cases above.

=================== #155
S2. Add a "Suggest change" button to the diff comment form by vvchopra 2026-11-11T04:49:11Z

### User Story

Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: small` · Type: Feature · Part of #151

As a reviewer, I want a button that fills in a suggestion block with the current line so that I
only edit the code instead of copying it and remembering the syntax.

### User Scenario

Ana opens the Files tab of an open PR and clicks the `+` next to new-side line 18. The code
comment form that opens has a "Suggest change" button in its toolbar. She clicks it and the
textarea gets a ```` ```suggestion ```` block holding line 18's current text, with the cursor at the
end of that line inside the block. She edits the line and clicks "Add single comment". The comment
is saved with the block as she typed it; showing it as a diff is S1's job.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given the code comment form opened on a new-side line (an added line, or an unchanged
  context line, including lines revealed by "expand"), in split or unified view, when the reviewer
  clicks "Suggest change", then the textarea contains a block made of a fence line
  ```` ```suggestion ````, the line's exact text (leading tabs and spaces kept, no `+` or space
  diff marker, no highlighting markup), and a closing fence.
- [ ] AC2: Given the textarea already has text, when the reviewer clicks "Suggest change", then the
  block is inserted at the cursor (replacing any selected text), starts on a line of its own and is
  followed by a newline, and the text before and after it is kept.
- [ ] AC3: Given the block was just inserted, then the textarea has focus and the cursor sits at
  the end of the line's text inside the block.
- [ ] AC4: Given the line's text contains a run of N backticks with N ≥ 3 (for example
  ```` ```js ````), when the block is inserted, then both fences use N+1 backticks, so the block
  is not closed early. With fewer than 3 backticks in a row, the fences stay at 3.
- [ ] AC5: Given an empty or whitespace-only line, when the block is inserted, then the block
  holds that line as is (an empty line or the same whitespace) between the fences.
- [ ] AC6: Given the form opened on an old-side line (a deleted line, or the left column of a
  changed line in split view), when the form is shown, then the "Suggest change" button is not
  shown. If the customer's answer to question 5 on #151 allows old-side suggestions, this AC is
  updated before coding starts.
- [ ] AC7: Given any markdown editor other than the code comment form (issue or PR conversation
  comment, review summary, editing an existing comment, a reply in an existing conversation), when
  it is shown, then it has no "Suggest change" button.
- [ ] AC8: Given a visitor who is not signed in, or a repository that is archived, when the Files
  tab is shown, then there is no code comment form and so no button (behaviour unchanged,
  regression test).
- [ ] AC9: Given a merged or closed PR, when the reviewer opens the code comment form, then the
  button is shown and works as in AC1 (Gitea still allows code comments there). If the customer
  answers that suggestions on closed PRs should be blocked, this AC is updated before coding.
- [ ] AC10: The button is a keyboard-focusable `<button>` with an accessible name and tooltip
  from a new locale key `repo.diff.comment.suggest_change` (English "Suggest change", added to
  `locale_en-US.json` only).
- [ ] AC11: Given a comment with a suggestion block, when it is submitted, then the stored comment
  content is exactly the textarea text (no server-side change to comment content).

### Out of Scope

- Selecting several lines (S5).
- Rendering the block as a diff (S1) and applying it (S3).
- The button in reply forms of an existing conversation. A line that already has a conversation
  has no `+`, so suggestions there wait for a later issue.
- The legacy EasyMDE editor: switching to it hides the button, and switching back shows it again.
- Server-side checks on suggestion blocks. The server stores them as plain markdown.

### Open Questions

- Customer question 5 on #151: are suggestions on the old (deleted) side allowed? AC6 assumes no.
- New question for the customer: should a reviewer be able to write a suggestion on a merged or
  closed PR, where it can never be applied? AC9 assumes yes, since the form is already there.

### Design Decision

**Decision:** Read the line text from the diff row already in the DOM (the `.code-inner` cell of
the row the form belongs to, as `textContent`) and insert it with the existing
`replaceTextareaSelection` helper from `EditorMarkdown.ts`; no server call. The button is added to
the shared markdown toolbar only when the editor sits inside a code comment form for the right
side.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Fetch the raw line from the server.* Exact, but a round trip for text already on the page, and a
  new endpoint with its own permission checks.
- *Server-render the block into the form's initial value.* Forces a suggestion on every comment and
  the reviewer has to delete it for a plain comment.

**Rationale:** The diff row holds the exact text the reviewer is looking at, which is what the
suggestion is anchored to.

**Consequences:** Depends on the diff row markup; highlighted spans must be read as plain text
(`textContent`), and an e2e test guards it. If the markup changes upstream, the e2e test fails
instead of the button inserting the wrong text.

### Decision 2

**Decision:** Build the fences from backticks, one longer than the longest backtick run in the line
and never shorter than 3. The text-building function is pure and unit-tested in Vitest.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Always use 3 backticks.* Breaks on any line holding ```` ``` ````, such as markdown files or
  code that embeds fenced blocks.
- *Use a tilde fence (`~~~suggestion`).* Fails the same way on lines holding `~~~`, and S1's
  renderer would need to accept both fence styles.

**Rationale:** CommonMark closes a fence only on a run at least as long as the opening one, so a
longer opening fence always holds the line, whatever it contains.

**Consequences:** S1's parser must accept suggestion fences longer than 3 backticks.

### Scope

small

### Scope Justification

Frontend only: one toolbar button in the shared markdown editor template shown for code comment
forms, a small TypeScript module with a pure text builder (Vitest) and the click handler, one
locale key, and one Playwright e2e test. No Go, database, API or permission changes.

--- comments

## PR #161: Gitar's finding is fixed and pushed

Gitar was right. Chrome on Android has a `Notification` object, but calling `new Notification()` there throws an error. In the polling fallback, that error happened before the next poll was scheduled. So after the first alert, the unread count and tab dot would stop updating until a page reload.

The fix is commit `d859485343`. It wraps the alert in a try/catch so a failed alert gets logged and polling carries on. It also adds tests, all written by me (Claude):
- **`notification-desktop.test.ts`:** one new test checking that `showDesktopAlert` doesn't throw when the browser refuses to create the alert.
- **`notification.test.ts` (new):** three tests for the polling path, which had no tests before:
  - a hidden tab alerts with the number of new notifications (AC5)
  - no alert when the tab is visible or the count goes down (AC7)
  - polling keeps going after a refused alert

I reverted the fix and reran the tests to make sure they catch the bug: the two refused-alert tests failed with the same "Illegal constructor" error Gitar described. With the fix, all 21 tests in the notification test files pass, and eslint, tsc and the whitespace check are clean.

**What else blocks the merge:**
- **Gitar's review thread is still open.** The repo won't merge with unresolved threads. Reply to it yourself, pointing at `d859485343`, and resolve it. The course doesn't allow AI-written replies on your own PR.
- **SonarCloud** failed on coverage: 78.3% of the new code was covered, and it needs 80%. The new polling tests should push it over, but that won't be confirmed until the rerun finishes.
- **The e2e failure wasn't caused by our code.** The CI machine failed to install Playwright's system packages. My push started a fresh run of every check.
- **A teammate still has to approve the latest commit.**

I've turned off email for activity on repos you're only watching, and it's still off after a page reload. That stops emails for PRs and issues you have no part in, like teammates' PRs in the course repo. They'll still show in your GitHub notifications inbox.

GitHub has no setting for "only issues and PRs I'm assigned to or opened." The other email setting, "Participating, @mentions and custom," is still on. Under that setting you'll still get emails for:
- issues and PRs you're assigned to or opened
- review requests
- @mentions
- any thread you've commented on

So after you post spec reviews on a teammate's issue, like #154 and #155, you'll keep getting emails about it. To stop those for one thread, click **Unsubscribe** in the right sidebar of that issue or PR.

I left the second setting on because turning it off would also stop emails for your own issues and PRs.
